@@ -0,0 +1,131 @@
+# Expanded generators and factorization lengths
+
+## Abstract
+
+Expanded generators refute Narayan's delta-set formula by unit-length normalization.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The expanded generating tuple).**
+
+$$\forall a \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall h \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall k \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall i \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(k + 2\right),\; \operatorname{generators}\left(a, h, d, k, i\right) = \operatorname{ite}\left(\operatorname{val}\left(i\right) = 0, a, a \cdot h + \left(\operatorname{val}\left(i\right) - 1\right) \cdot d\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.generators` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ashwin Narayan (2026). *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Conjecture 18.3 (p. 22) states: “For Sₕ =⟨a,ah,ah+d,ah+2d,...ah+kd ⟩, Δ(Sₕ) = E(e,d)”. The index i : Fin (k + 2) retains a at zero and ah at one. All later coordinates are ah + (i.val − 1)d; no displayed generator is removed.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Coordinate factorizations).**
+
+$$\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall g \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right) \to \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{Z}\left(g, n\right) = \{z : \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right) \to \mathbb{N} \mid \sum_{i : \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right)} (z\left(i\right) \cdot g\left(i\right)) = n\}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.Z` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ashwin Narayan (2026). *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Section 3 (p. 2) states: “Suppose the set of factorizations of n ∈ S is given by Z(n) = { (z₁, z₂, …, zₚ) ∈ ℕᵖ ∣ z₁ n₁ + z₂ n₂ + … + zₚ nₚ = n }”. The p coordinates are indexed from zero by Fin p and take nonnegative integer values, including zero as in the paper's subsequent inequalities. The sum is over every coordinate.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Length sets).**
+
+$$\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall g \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right) \to \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{L}\left(g, n\right) = \operatorname{Set}.\operatorname{image}\left(\operatorname{fun} (z : \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right) \to \mathbb{N}) \mapsto \sum_{i : \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right)} (z\left(i\right)), \operatorname{Z}\left(g, n\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.L` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ashwin Narayan (2026). *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Section 3 (p. 3) states: “If z = (z₁, z₂, z₃, …, zₚ) is a factorization of n, then the length of z is given by |z| = z₁ + z₂ + z₃ + … + zₚ”. It continues: “The set of lengths of n is defined by L(n) = {|z| | z ∈ Z(n)} ⊂ ℕ”. Set.image applies the coordinate sum to all factorizations of n.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Positive consecutive length differences).**
+
+$$\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall g \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right) \to \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{delta}\left(g\right) = \{q : \mathbb{N} \mid \exists n \in \mathbb{N},\; \exists lone \in \mathbb{N},\; \exists ltwo \in \mathbb{N},\; (lone \in \operatorname{L}\left(g, n\right)) \land ((ltwo \in \operatorname{L}\left(g, n\right)) \land ((lone < ltwo) \land ((q = ltwo - lone) \land (\forall l \in \mathbb{N},\; (l \in \operatorname{L}\left(g, n\right)) \Rightarrow (\neg ((lone < l) \land (l < ltwo)))))))\}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.delta` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ashwin Narayan (2026). *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Definition 3.1 (p. 3) states: “We define the delta set as Δ(Sₕ) = { l₂ − l₁ : l₂,l₁ ∈ L(s), L(s) ∩ (l₁,l₂) = ∅ }”. Here s ranges over all represented natural numbers and l₁ < l₂, so differences are positive and the endpoints are distinct. The final quantified clause excludes every intermediate length. Subtraction is natural-number subtraction.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Subtractive Euclidean step).**
+
+$$\forall s \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{euclidStep}\left(s\right) = \operatorname{ite}\left(\operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{snd}\left(s\right) < \operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{fst}\left(s\right), (\operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{fst}\left(s\right) - \operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{snd}\left(s\right), \operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{snd}\left(s\right)), \operatorname{ite}\left(\operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{fst}\left(s\right) < \operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{snd}\left(s\right), (\operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{fst}\left(s\right), \operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{snd}\left(s\right) - \operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{fst}\left(s\right)), s\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.euclidStep` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ashwin Narayan (2026). *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Definition 3.2 (p. 3) states: “We define the subtractive Euclidean Algorithm in this way: Let x₀ and y₀ = (e,d)” and “Recursively define” the next pair as (xᵢ−yᵢ,yᵢ) if xᵢ>yᵢ, (xᵢ,yᵢ−xᵢ) if yᵢ>xᵢ, and “terminate” if xᵢ=yᵢ. The function ite selects its second argument when its first argument holds and its third otherwise. The equal pair is stationary; Prod.fst and Prod.snd are its coordinates.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Euclidean states).**
+
+$$\forall e \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; (\operatorname{euclidState}\left(e, d, 0\right) = (e, d)) \land (\forall i \in \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{euclidState}\left(e, d, i + 1\right) = \operatorname{euclidStep}\left(\operatorname{euclidState}\left(e, d, i\right)\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.euclidState` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ashwin Narayan (2026). *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Definition 3.2 (p. 3) starts with (x₀,y₀)=(e,d) and applies the displayed subtractive step recursively. Retaining the final diagonal pair repeats a state already visited and adds no positive coordinate value.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (Values visited by the Euclidean algorithm).**
+
+$$\forall e \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{E}\left(e, d\right) = \{q : \mathbb{N} \mid (0 < q) \land (\exists i \in \mathbb{N},\; (\operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{fst}\left(\operatorname{euclidState}\left(e, d, i\right)\right) = q) \lor (\operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{snd}\left(\operatorname{euclidState}\left(e, d, i\right)\right) = q))\}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.E` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ashwin Narayan (2026). *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The abstract (p. 1) states: “Writing e=h−1 and letting E(e,d) denote the set of values arising from the subtractive Euclidean algorithm applied to e and d”. The set contains the positive coordinates of all states, including the initial and terminal states.
+
+**Definition 1.8 (Conjecture 18.3).**
+
+$$\operatorname{claim} = (\forall a \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall h \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall k \in \mathbb{N},\; (0 < a) \Rightarrow ((0 < h) \Rightarrow ((0 < d) \Rightarrow ((0 < k) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Coprime}\left(a, d\right)) \Rightarrow ((1 < k) \Rightarrow ((k < a) \Rightarrow ((1 < h) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{delta}\left(\operatorname{generators}\left(a, h, d, k\right)\right) = \operatorname{E}\left(h - 1, d\right))))))))))$$
+

+
+## Abstract
+
+Actual Normal-Current Boundary Expansion
+
+The actual current is H_i(m)+beta_i delta(m,0). At conformal index m the normal-product coefficient is m+1. +open scoped BigOperators

+/-- The tuple (a, a*h, a*h+d, ..., a*h+k*d), with every coordinate retained. -/
+def generators (a h d k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)) : ℕ :=
+  if i.val = 0 then a else a * h + (i.val - 1) * d
+
+/-- The source's coordinate set Z(n), for a displayed tuple of p generators. -/
+def Z {p : ℕ} (g : Fin p → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Set (Fin p → ℕ) :=
+  {z | ∑ i, z i * g i = n}
+
+/-- The source's length set L(n). -/
+def L {p : ℕ} (g : Fin p → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
+  (fun z : Fin p → ℕ => ∑ i, z i) '' Z g n
+
+/-- The union over represented n of positive consecutive distinct length gaps. -/
+def delta {p : ℕ} (g : Fin p → ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
+  {q | ∃ n l₁ l₂ : ℕ, l₁ ∈ L g n ∧ l₂ ∈ L g n ∧ l₁ < l₂ ∧
+    q = l₂ - l₁ ∧ ∀ l : ℕ, l ∈ L g n → ¬ (l₁ < l ∧ l < l₂)}
+
+/-- One step of Definition 3.2; the diagonal is the terminating state. -/
+def euclidStep (s : ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ :=
+  if s.2 < s.1 then (s.1 - s.2, s.2)
+  else if s.1 < s.2 then (s.1, s.2 - s.1)
+  else s
+
+/-- Definition 3.2, with (x₀,y₀)=(e,d). -/
+def euclidState (e d : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ
+  | 0 => (e, d)
+  | i + 1 => euclidStep (euclidState e d i)
+
+/-- Positive coordinates encountered by the subtractive Euclidean algorithm. -/
+def E (e d : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
+  {q | 0 < q ∧ ∃ i : ℕ,
+    (euclidState e d i).1 = q ∨ (euclidState e d i).2 = q}
+
+/-- Conjecture 18.3, for all positive parameters under the Section 3 restrictions. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ a h d k : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < h → 0 < d → 0 < k →
+    Nat.Coprime a d → 1 < k → k < a → 1 < h →
+      delta (generators a h d k) = E (h - 1) d
+

+private def b (a : ℕ) (i : Fin a) : ℕ := 2 * a + 2 * i.val
+
+private def value {a : ℕ} (c : (ℕ × List (Fin a))) : ℕ :=
+  a * c.1 + (c.2.map (b a)).sum
+
+private def size {a : ℕ} (c : (ℕ × List (Fin a))) : ℕ := c.1 + c.2.length
+
+private def Terminal {a : ℕ} (c : (ℕ × List (Fin a))) : Prop :=
+  c.2 = [] ∨ ∃ i : Fin a, 0 < i.val ∧ c.2 = [i]
+
+private inductive Rewrite {a : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) : (ℕ × List (Fin a)) → (ℕ × List (Fin a)) → Prop

+  | small (x : ℕ) (i j : Fin a) (s : List (Fin a)) (h : i.val + j.val < a) :
+      Rewrite ha (x, i :: j :: s) (x + 2, ⟨i.val + j.val, h⟩ :: s)

+      Rewrite ha (x, i :: j :: s)

+private theorem rewrite_value {a : ℕ} {ha : 0 < a} {c d : (ℕ × List (Fin a))}

+  | zero x s => simp [value, b, Nat.mul_add]; omega
+  | small x i j s h => simp [value, b, Nat.mul_add]; omega
+  | large x i j s h => simp [value, b]; omega
+
+private theorem rewrite_size {a : ℕ} {ha : 0 < a} {c d : (ℕ × List (Fin a))}
+    (h : Rewrite ha c d) : size d = size c + 1 := by
+  cases h <;> simp [size] <;> omega
+
+private theorem size_le_value {a : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (c : (ℕ × List (Fin a))) :

+  rcases c with ⟨x, s⟩
+  have hs : s.length ≤ (s.map (b a)).sum := by

+      obtain ⟨i, _, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hn
+      dsimp [b]
+      omega)
+    simpa using h
+  have hx := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left x ha
+  dsimp [size, value]
+  omega

+private theorem terminal_or_step {a : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (c : (ℕ × List (Fin a))) :

+  cases s with
+  | nil => exact Or.inl (Or.inl rfl)
+  | cons i s =>

+    | nil =>

+        exact ⟨_, Rewrite.zero x []⟩
+      · exact Or.inl (Or.inr ⟨i, Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hi, rfl⟩)
+    | cons j s =>

+      by_cases h : i.val + j.val < a
+      · exact ⟨_, Rewrite.small x i j s h⟩
+      · exact ⟨_, Rewrite.large x i j s (Nat.le_of_not_gt h)⟩

+      have hb := size_le_value ha d

+      exact ⟨t, ht, (Relation.ReflTransGen.single hd).trans hreach⟩

+    (h : Relation.ReflTransGen (Rewrite ha) c d) :

+  | refl => exact ⟨rfl, le_rfl, fun l hl hu => ⟨_, rfl, by omega⟩⟩
+  | @tail d e hreach hstep ih =>
+    have hv := rewrite_value hstep
+    have hs := rewrite_size hstep
+    refine ⟨hv.trans ih.1, by omega, ?_⟩
+    intro l hl hu
+    by_cases hd : l ≤ size d
+    · exact ih.2.2 l hl hd
+    · exact ⟨e, hv.trans ih.1, by omega⟩
+
+private theorem cancel_residue {a r s : ℕ} (hc : Nat.Coprime a 2)
+    (hr : r < a) (hs : s < a) (h : (2 * r) % a = (2 * s) % a) : r = s := by
+  have he : Nat.ModEq a (2 * r) (2 * s) := h
+  have he' := Nat.ModEq.cancel_left_of_coprime hc he

+private theorem terminal_unique {a : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hc : Nat.Coprime a 2)
+    {c d : (ℕ × List (Fin a))} (htc : Terminal c) (htd : Terminal d)

+  rcases c with ⟨x, s⟩
+  rcases d with ⟨y, t⟩

+    rcases htd with ht | ⟨j, hj, ht⟩
+  · dsimp only [Prod.snd] at hs ht

+      ⁅sugawaraMode D H m + shiftCurrent D u m +
+          (if m=0 then halfNorm D u else 0) • (1 : Module.End ℂ (Carrier D)),
+        sugawaraMode D H n + shiftCurrent D u n +
+          (if n=0 then halfNorm D u else 0) • (1 : Module.End ℂ (Carrier D))⁆ =
+      ⁅sugawaraMode D H m,sugawaraMode D H n⁆ +
+        ⁅sugawaraMode D H m,shiftCurrent D u n⁆ +
+        ⁅shiftCurrent D u m,sugawaraMode D H n⁆ +
+        ⁅shiftCurrent D u m,shiftCurrent D u n⁆ := by
+    simp only [Ring.lie_def,add_mul,mul_add,smul_mul_assoc,mul_smul_comm,
+      mul_one,one_mul,smul_smul]
+    module
+  rw [expansion,hb,base_shift_commutator D H hHG hGH,ho,shift_shift_commutator]
+  have hk : (∑ i,∑ j,u i*(D.G i j : ℂ)*u j) = 2*halfNorm D u := by
+    unfold halfNorm
+    ring
+  rw [hk]

+  · have hn : (n : ℂ)=-(m : ℂ) := by
+      have : n = -m := by omega
+      simp [this]
+    simp only [hmn,ite_true,Int.cast_sub,hn]
+    module
+  · simp only [hmn,ite_false,zero_smul,add_zero,Int.cast_sub]
+    module
+
+end

+
+# Expanded generating tuples and delta sets
+
+## Verified locator
+
+DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495
+
+Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1
+
+## Source statements
+
+Conjecture 18.3, p. 22, states: “For Sₕ =⟨a,ah,ah+d,ah+2d,...ah+kd ⟩, Δ(Sₕ) = E(e,d)”.
+Its source TeX is:
+
+```tex
+For \[S_h =\langle a,ah,ah+d,ah+2d,...ah+kd \rangle,\]
+\[\Delta(S_h) = E(e,d) \]
+```
+
+Section 3, p. 2, assumes “gcd(a,d) =1, 1<k<a, h > 1” and sets “e =h−1.”
+It states: “Suppose the set of factorizations of n ∈ S is given by
+Z(n) = { (z₁, z₂, …, zₚ) ∈ ℕᵖ ∣ z₁ n₁ + z₂ n₂ + … + zₚ nₚ = n }”.
+On p. 3: “If z = (z₁, z₂, z₃, …, zₚ) is a factorization of n, then the length of z is given by
+|z| = z₁ + z₂ + z₃ + … + zₚ”. It continues: “The set of lengths of n is defined by
+L(n) = {|z| | z ∈ Z(n)} ⊂ ℕ”.
+
+Definition 3.1, p. 3, states: “We define the delta set as
+Δ(Sₕ) = { l₂ − l₁ : l₂,l₁ ∈ L(s), L(s) ∩ (l₁,l₂) = ∅ }”.
+Definition 3.2, p. 3, states: “We define the subtractive Euclidean Algorithm in this way: Let
+x₀ and y₀ = (e,d)” and “Recursively define” the next pair as (xᵢ−yᵢ,yᵢ) if xᵢ>yᵢ,
+(xᵢ,yᵢ−xᵢ) if yᵢ>xᵢ, and “terminate” if xᵢ=yᵢ.
+The abstract, p. 1, states: “Writing e=h−1 and letting E(e,d) denote the set of values
+arising from the subtractive Euclidean algorithm applied to e and d”.
+
+## Mathematical scope
+
+Factorizations retain all coordinates of the displayed tuple, including the redundant ah.
+Coordinates are nonnegative integers as in the source's subsequent factorization inequalities.
+The delta set is the union, over represented natural numbers, of positive gaps between distinct
+successive lengths. This supplies the unbound s and the omitted endpoint ordering in Definition 3.1.
+The initialization is (x₀,y₀)=(e,d). Keeping the terminal diagonal pair stationary adds no
+new visited positive coordinate. These readings are fixed in issue #23185.
+
+For (a,h,d,k)=(3,2,2,2), the expanded tuple is (3,6,8,10). The repository's argument proves
+that for every positive a coprime to 2, all represented length sets for
+(a,2a,2a+2,…,4a−2) are integer intervals and its delta set is {1}.
+The relation 2a=a+a and the pair-replacement rules yield complete paths with unit length
+increments. Residues modulo a determine their common terminal endpoint. The initial value
+2 belongs to E(1,2), contradicting Conjecture 18.3. The tuple omitting ah has different
+factorizations; the paper's main theorem for it and catenary Conjectures 18.1–18.2 are outside
+this conclusion.
+
+## Experiment and literature boundary
+
+The exact-arithmetic checker is in `the-omega-institute/trureturing-experiments`, commit
+`23c744d471f53c63a530ec05520a55c2902f2050`, at
+`docs/reports/numerical-monoid-delta-set/check.py`, SHA-256
+`6e39c9873b672007c385e46c4af6973fd500dbe17f6b37dc47fe46a2da1ab89a`.
+The command `python3 docs/reports/numerical-monoid-delta-set/check.py` is reported in

+The source assertion is literature-attested; the family-specific completeness argument is

+and the literature screen. Completeness of later-citation, web and MathDB coverage, and the

+**Theorem 10.1 (A genuine family with gap of order $r^{3/2}$).** For every integer $a\ge4$, put $r=a+1$, $s=a+2$, $H=[a+1]$ and $e=a+2$. For each real $0<\varepsilon\le1/a$, define the one array
+
+$$
+x_{\{e\}}=\varepsilon,\qquad x_H=(a-1)\varepsilon,\qquad
+x_{H\setminus\{j\}}=\frac{1-a\varepsilon}{a+1}\quad(j\in H),
+$$
+
+with every other type mass zero. This is an actual profile of mean $q=a$ with positive marginals. Its support hypergraph, with vertices $[s]$ and hyperedges the positive-mass types, has two connected components. Define
+
+$$
+E_a=2a^3-2a-1,\qquad A_a=2a^3+2a^2-2a-1.
+$$
+
+Its energy and gap are exactly
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)=\frac{(a+1)^2[a^3+\varepsilon E_a]}{(a-\varepsilon)^2}
++\frac1\varepsilon,\tag{10.1}
+$$
+
+$$
+2\bigl(J_s(x)-F_r(a)\bigr)
+=\frac1\varepsilon+
+\frac{(a+1)^2\varepsilon(A_a-a\varepsilon)}{(a-\varepsilon)^2}>0.\tag{10.2}
+$$
+
+For $\varepsilon_a=1/(\sqrt2\,a^{3/2})$ the limit is
+
+$$
+\frac{J_s(x(\varepsilon_a))-F_{a+1}(a)}{a^{3/2}}
+\longrightarrow\sqrt2,
+\qquad
+\frac{J_s(x(\varepsilon_a))-F_{a+1}(a)}{(a+1)^{3/2}}
+\longrightarrow\sqrt2.\tag{10.3}
+$$
+
+Thus no constant $c>0$ can satisfy $J_s(x)-F_r(q)\ge cr^2$ uniformly for all integers $r\ge5$, all finite $s\ge r+1$ and all actual profiles with $q\in[r-1,r]$.
+
+**Proof.** The displayed masses are nonnegative and sum to
+
+$$
+\varepsilon+(a-1)\varepsilon+1-a\varepsilon=1.
+$$
+
+Their cardinality mean is
+
+$$
+\varepsilon+(a+1)(a-1)\varepsilon+a(1-a\varepsilon)=a.
+$$
+
+Counting the types containing each hub gives
+
+$$
+y_i=\frac{a-\varepsilon}{a+1}>0\quad(i\in H),\qquad
+y_e=\varepsilon>0,
+$$
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+w_i&=\frac{a^3(1-a\varepsilon)}{a+1}
+ +(a+1)^2(a-1)\varepsilon
+ =\frac{a^3+\varepsilon E_a}{a+1}\quad(i\in H),\\
+w_e&=\varepsilon.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+In particular the extra marginal is retained. The only positive-mass type containing $e$ is $\{e\}$, while $H$ itself has positive mass. No positive-mass type meets both $H$ and $\{e\}$, so the incidence support has these two components. This remains true at $\varepsilon=1/a$, where all missing-one masses are zero; the core marginals remain positive there.
+
+Summing $w_i/y_i^2$ gives (10.1). Since $2F_r(a)=a(a+1)^2$, subtraction gives (10.2). Its denominator is positive. Moreover $a\varepsilon\le1$ and $A_a>1$ for $a\ge4$, so both summands are strictly positive. Hence these arrays do not improve or tie the candidate.
+
+The choice $\varepsilon_a$ lies in $(0,1/a]$. Dividing (10.2) by $2a^{3/2}$ gives
+
+$$
+\frac{J_s(x(\varepsilon_a))-F_r(a)}{a^{3/2}}
+=\frac1{\sqrt2}
++\frac{(1+1/a)^2\bigl(A_a/a^3-\varepsilon_a/a^2\bigr)}
+ {2\sqrt2(1-\varepsilon_a/a)^2}.
+$$
+
+As $a\to\infty$, the second term tends to $1/\sqrt2$, proving the first limit in (10.3). The second follows from $a/(a+1)\to1$. A wholly rational infinite subfamily is
+
+$$
+a=2b^2,\qquad \varepsilon=\frac1{4b^3},\qquad b\in\mathbb Z,\ b\ge2;
+$$
+
+it has exactly the same limit. Thus the gap divided by $r^2$ tends to zero through actual positive-marginal arrays. For any proposed $c>0$, a sufficiently large member violates the asserted uniform lower bound. ∎
+
+The formulas (10.1)–(10.3) do not assert that these arrays minimize $J_s$, or determine the largest positive gap for any fixed $r$. They restrict the possible scale of a uniform all-$r$ gap. The exact array family has disconnected support; it is not itself a connected finite graph construction at every prescribed budget. Theorem 7.1 can realize a fixed profile asymptotically under its stated budget hypotheses, but does not identify the finite optimum or transfer (10.2) to every integer graph budget.

+**Lemma 13.6 (Necessary structure at the sharp scale).** Under the hypotheses of Lemma 13.5, suppose in addition that
+$$
+\frac{d(x_a)}{a^{3/2}}\longrightarrow2\sqrt2\,h.
+\tag{13.14}
+$$
+Then, for every choice of $h$ smallest-marginal labels,
+$$
+ a^{3/2}p\longrightarrow\frac h{\sqrt2},\qquad
+ a^{3/2}t_j\longrightarrow\frac1{\sqrt2}\quad(j\in D),
+\tag{13.15}
+$$
+$$
+\mathbb E[K^2\mid A]\longrightarrow1,\qquad
+\frac{x_{\{j\}}}{t_j}\longrightarrow1\quad(j\in D),\qquad
+\min_{i\in C}y_i\longrightarrow1.
+\tag{13.16}
+$$
+In particular $u/p\to1$, and conditioned on $A$ the tail count is one with probability tending to one.
+
+**Proof.** The refined lower bound (13.10), followed by (13.12), gives
+$$
+\frac{d(x_a)}{a^{3/2}}
+\ge\frac{h^2}{\pi_a}+(2+o(1))\pi_a,
+\qquad \pi_a=a^{3/2}p.
+$$
+By (13.9), $\pi_a$ is bounded above, and (13.12) together with the bound on $H_D$ in (13.9) bounds it away from zero. The function $h^2/\pi+2\pi$ has minimum $2\sqrt2h$, attained only at $\pi=h/\sqrt2$. Therefore (13.14) forces $\pi_a\to h/\sqrt2$. The same inequalities then force
+$$
+\frac{H_D}{a^{3/2}}\to\sqrt2h,\qquad pH_D\to h^2.
+\tag{13.17}
+$$
+Let $\mathbb E_A$ denote conditional expectation on $A$. Since $H_D=p\mathbb E_A W$ and $\mathbb E_A V=h/p$, conditional Cauchy--Schwarz gives $p^2\mathbb E_A V^2\ge h^2$. Thus (13.17) gives
+$$
+0\le p^2\mathbb E_A(W-V^2)
+=pH_D-p^2\mathbb E_A V^2\le pH_D-h^2\longrightarrow0.
+$$
+On $A$, every $t_j\le p$, so $V\ge1/p$. Since $K\ge B$ and $1\le B\le h$,
+$$
+\frac{K^2}{B}-1\ge\frac{K^2-1}{h+1}.
+$$
+The within-type Cauchy inequality therefore gives
+$$
+W-V^2\ge\left(\frac{K^2}{B}-1\right)V^2
+\ge\frac{K^2-1}{(h+1)p^2}.
+$$
+Consequently
+$$
+0\le\mathbb E_A(K^2-1)

+
+$$

+p_{\mathrm{low}}=\sum_{|T|\le r-2}x_T.
+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+\Delta\ge3(r-1)p_{\mathrm{low}}
++\frac{(r-1)^2}{2}\sum_{i=1}^r\left(y_i-\frac qr\right)^2,\tag{3.1}
+$$
+
+$$
+\|x-x^*(q)\|_1
+\le\frac{\sqrt{2r}}{r-1}\sqrt\Delta+\frac23\Delta.\tag{3.2}
+$$
+
+Equality $J_r(x)=F_r(q)$ holds exactly for $x=x^*(q)$, including $q=r-1$ and $q=r$.

+**Proof.** The following type identity is the intermediate structure needed for the estimates, rather than an assumption of equal marginals. For $\theta=q-a$ define
+
+$$
+R_i=w_i-a^2y_i-(2r-1)\theta.
+$$
+
+Expansion separately over types containing and avoiding $i$ gives
+
+$$
+R_i=\sum_{T\not\ni i}(2r-1)(r-|T|-1)x_T
++\sum_{T\ni i}(r-|T|)(r-|T|-1)x_T.\tag{3.3}
+$$
+
+All occurring coefficients are nonnegative: a type avoiding $i$ has $|T|\le r-1$, and the other product vanishes at $|T|=r-1,r$. For a type of cardinality $k\le r-2$, its coefficient in $\sum_iR_i$ is
+
+$$
+(r-k)(r-k-1)(2r-1+k)\ge6(r-1).
+$$
+
+To verify the last inequality for all such integers, set $z=r-k\in\{2,\ldots,r-1\}$. The expression is $z(z-1)(3r-z-1)$; its increment from $z$ to $z+1$ is $3z(2r-z-1)>0$, and its value at $z=2$ is $6(r-1)$. Since $y_i\le1$,
+
+$$
+J_r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^rh_\theta(y_i)+\frac12\sum_i\frac{R_i}{y_i^2}
+\ge\sum_i h_\theta(y_i)+3a p_{\mathrm{low}},
+$$
+
+$$
+h_\theta(y)=\frac{a^2}{2y}+\frac{(2r-1)\theta}{2y^2},\qquad
+h_\theta''(y)=\frac{a^2}{y^3}+\frac{3(2r-1)\theta}{y^4}\ge a^2
+\quad(0<y\le1).
+$$
+
+The ordinary strong-convexity inequality, summed at $y=q/r$ using $\sum_i(y_i-q/r)=0$, yields
+
+$$

++\frac{a^2}{2}\sum_i(y_i-q/r)^2.
+$$

+
+$$
+p=p_{\mathrm{low}},\qquad
+\varepsilon=\sum_{|T|\le a-1}(a-|T|)x_T,\qquad
+l_i=\sum_{\substack{|T|\le a-1\\i\notin T}}x_T.
+$$

+The mean identity implies $x_{[r]}=\theta+\varepsilon$, and the marginal identity implies
+
+$$
+x_{[r]\setminus\{i\}}-\frac{r-q}{r}
+=-(y_i-q/r)-l_i.

+&\le\sum_i|y_i-q/r|+2\varepsilon+2p\\

+**Theorem 7.2 (Capacity-constrained density limit and necessary and sufficient near-minimum structure).** Fix either admissible class of Theorem 6.1 and a prescribed integer sequence $\ell_n$ with
+
+$$
+L_r(n)\le\ell_n\le U_r(n)\text{ eventually},\qquad
+\frac{\ell_n}{n}\longrightarrow\alpha\in[r-2,r-1].
+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+nE_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)\longrightarrow F_r(1+\alpha).\tag{7.1}
+$$
+
+For any sequence $G_n\in\mathcal A_r(n,\ell_n)$, the following are equivalent:
+
+1. $E(G_n)-E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)=o(1/n)$;
+2. $nE(G_n)\to F_r(1+\alpha)$;
+3. eventually $G_n$ is an actual two-layer graph with exactly $r$ degree-oriented sinks, and, for its source counts and hub degrees with $N=n-r$,
+
+$$
+\frac1N\sum_{|T|\le r-2}a_T\longrightarrow0,\qquad
+\frac{D_i}{N}-\frac{q_r}{r}\longrightarrow0\quad(1\le i\le r),
+\qquad q_r=\frac{n-1+\ell_n}{n-r};\tag{7.2}
+$$
+
+4. eventually $G_n$ has exactly those $r$ actual sinks and source–sink structure, and its single profile satisfies
+
+$$
+\|x^{(n)}-x^*(q_r)\|_1\longrightarrow0.\tag{7.3}
+$$
+
+In the unrestricted class this includes $r=9$ with every $\alpha\in[7,8]$, and $r=10$ with every $\alpha\in[8,9]$; for general $r\ge5$ the second class retains its minimum-degree hypothesis. Labels of the $r$ sinks may be chosen separately at each order; the limiting candidate is permutation invariant. In particular every hub degree divided by $n$ tends to $(1+\alpha)/r$. These conclusions allow $o(n)$ low-cardinality sources and unbounded sublinear hub imbalances. They do not assert finite disappearance of exceptional sources or a bounded difference of hub degrees.
+
+**Proof.** Theorem 6.1 gives the exact minimum at every sufficiently large order. For its balanced graph, $q_r\to1+\alpha$, $y_i=q_r/r+O(1/N)$, and the actual-edge error (6.3) together with (5.2) gives
+
+$$
+E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)=\frac{F_r(q_r)}N+O_r(n^{-3}).\tag{7.4}
+$$
+
+Since $n/N\to1$, this proves (7.1) and the equivalence of 1 and 2.
+
+Assume 1. The limit is bounded by $r^3/2$, because $F_r$ increases to $F_r(r)=r^3/2$. Thus $E(G_n)\le C_0/n$ eventually. The fixed-cost reduction of the sink-incidence volume, Theorem 3.1, applies to these actual graphs. It supplies their two-layer structure, a bounded number of sinks and the positive bound $D_i/n\ge1/(3C_0)$ for every actual sink. Capacity supplies $s\ge r$; no hub with a vanishing normalized degree has been suppressed. If $s>r$ along any infinite subsequence, (6.5) gives
+
+$$
+\liminf n\bigl(E(G_n)-E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)\bigr)\ge\widehat\gamma>0
+$$
+
+on that subsequence, contradicting 1. This exclusion uses (3.6) or (4.2) when $q_s>r$, so it remains valid at $\alpha=r-1$. Eventually $s=r$.
+
+For the actual $r$-sink array let $\Delta_n=J_r(x^{(n)})-F_r(q_r)\ge0$. Equations (6.3) and (7.4) imply
+
+$$
+\Delta_n=N\bigl(E(G_n)-E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)\bigr)+O_r(n^{-2})\longrightarrow0.
+$$
+
+Theorem 3.1 yields (7.2) and (7.3), including the explicit estimate (3.2). This proves 3 and 4. Conversely 3 implies 4 directly from (3.4), independently of a presumed small energy gap.
+
+Finally assume 4. Then every marginal tends to $(1+\alpha)/r>0$, so the bounded source degrees and positive linear hub degrees allow the actual-edge expansion. The functional $J_r$ is continuous there, and $x^*(q_r)\to x^*(1+\alpha)$, hence
+
+$$
+nE(G_n)=\frac nN J_r(x^{(n)})+O_r(n^{-2})\longrightarrow F_r(1+\alpha).
+$$
+
+This proves 2 and completes all equivalences.
+
+The endpoint capacity hypotheses cannot be replaced by their density limits: $\alpha$ alone does not specify the least feasible integer hub count. At $\alpha=r-2$ the candidate full mass tends to zero, but its exact count is still $c\ge r$ at every finite order, connecting the entire construction. At $\alpha=r-1$ the missing-one masses may vanish, and $b=0$ gives an actual complete bipartite graph. All proofs above allow these zero-mass limits. ∎

+**Theorem 11.3 (Unrestricted profile comparison at every capacity phase).** For every integer $r\ge5$, every finite $s\ge r$ and every profile of Definition 1.1 with $q\in[r-1,r]$,
+
+$$
+J_s(x)\ge F_r(q).
+$$
+
+Equality holds exactly for $s=r$ and $x=x^*(q)$, up to relabeling. If $s>r$, its common datum satisfies the stronger bound (11.2), in particular
+
+$$
+J_s(x)\ge F_r(q)+(r-1)+\frac1{2r}.\tag{11.6}
+$$
+
+For arbitrary $q\ge r$, every profile with finite $s\ge r+1$ also satisfies, for each $2\le\beta\le\kappa_r$,
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge r^3+\beta(s-r)+(D-\beta)(q-r).
+\tag{11.7}
+$$
+
+Here $D-\beta>0$; in particular $\beta=2$ gives $J_s(x)\ge r^3/2+1$. The bound (11.7) does not require $q\le r$.
+
+The interval comparison includes every $r\ge11$ and every mean in Definition 8.3, without the support hypothesis of Theorem 4.1 or the upper-density restriction of Theorem 8.1. It extends the comparison and equality statement of Theorem 3.2 to all $r\ge5$. Its domain is $s\ge r$; at $q=r-1$ it does not exclude the separate class $s=r-1$.
+
+**Proof.** If $s>r$, Definition 11.1 transfers the profile to one common datum, and Theorem 11.2 applies. If $s=r$, Theorem 3.1 supplies the inequality and its complete equality class, including both endpoints. This uses the existing fixed-$r$ equality theorem without any hypothesis on low cardinalities.
+
+For (11.7), apply Theorem 2.1 on its unrestricted mean domain. Since $f_r(r)=r^3$,
+
+$$
+f_r(q)+\beta(s-q)
+=r^3+\beta(s-r)+(D-\beta)(q-r).
+$$
+
+The admissible range of $\beta$ is nonempty, since $\kappa_r\ge2$. As proved in Theorem 2.1, $\kappa_r\le2a^2<D$, so the last coefficient is positive. For $s\ge r+1$ and $q\ge r$, taking $\beta=2$ gives the asserted gap above $r^3/2$. ∎
+

+---
+slug: narayan-delta-set
+bibkey: narayan2026deltaset
+doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2610.02495
+url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1
+triage: theorem
+motivation_gids:
+  - D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.result
+---
+
+# Narayan's expanded-generator delta-set conjecture
+
+## Problem
+
+Ashwin Narayan, *The Delta Set of a Numerical Monoid Generated by a Generalized Arithmetic Sequence*, [arXiv:2610.02495v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02495v1), Conjecture 18.3, p. 22, states:
+
+> For $S_h=\langle a,ah,ah+d,ah+2d,\ldots,ah+kd\rangle$, $\Delta(S_h)=E(e,d)$.
+
+Section 3 assumes $\gcd(a,d)=1$, $1<k<a$, $h>1$, and puts $e=h-1$. All four parameters are positive integers. Every displayed generator, including the redundant $ah$, is retained as a separate nonnegative factorization coordinate. The delta set is the union over represented natural numbers of positive differences between consecutive distinct lengths. The subtractive Euclidean algorithm starts at $(e,d)$; its final equal pair may be repeated without adding visited positive coordinates. These interpretations resolve the unbound $s$, omitted endpoint order and malformed initialization in Definitions 3.1–3.2, as fixed by [#23185](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23185).
+
+### Statement echo
+
+| Source clause | Lean counterpart | Fidelity |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| All positive $a,h,d,k$ | The four natural-number binders and four positivity premises of `claim` | No parameter restriction is omitted. |
+| $\gcd(a,d)=1$, $1<k<a$, $h>1$ | `Nat.Coprime a d` and the three strict inequalities of `claim` | Literal restrictions. |
+| $(a,ah,ah+d,\ldots,ah+kd)$ | `generators`, indexed by `Fin (k + 2)` | The $ah$ coordinate is retained. |
+| Nonnegative coordinate factorizations with weighted sum $n$ | `Z` | The complete coordinate equation is retained. |
+| Length is the coordinate sum; $L(n)$ contains all such lengths | The image in `L` | No minimal-generator substitution. |
+| Positive successive length differences, over represented $n$ | `delta` | Strict endpoint order and no intermediate member are explicit. |
+| Subtractive Euclidean states and visited positive coordinates | `euclidStep`, `euclidState`, `E` | The initial and terminal coordinates are included. |
+| $\Delta(S_h)=E(h-1,d)$ | The equality in `claim`; `result` proves its universal assertion false | The witness is $(3,2,2,2)$. |
+
+The displayed finite sums use Mathlib directly; no separate coordinate-sum alias is introduced. The implementation carrier is a product of a natural number and a finite list. Every public definition displays its complete body in the Blueprint. There are no additional source-independent hypotheses in the public claim.
+
+## Motivation
+
+The settling GID is `D5/S3/Arith/Additive/NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.result`, with `admission_basis: open-problem-resolution (#23185; Refuted)`. The source note is [narayan2026deltaset](../Library/Factorization/narayan2026deltaset.md). The Scribe attaches exactly one Refuted `OpenProblemResolutionClaim` to that settling theorem.
+
+## Gap
+
+Adding $ah$ changes factorization lengths despite leaving the generated monoid unchanged. In particular, $2a$ admits both a single $2a$ coordinate and two $a$ coordinates. A finite calculation cannot exclude larger gaps at larger represented values. The proof therefore establishes complete normalization and intermediate-length realization for the whole family, without a cutoff in the represented value.
+
+## Route
+
+For $a>0$ coprime to $2$, put $b_i=2a+2i$ for $0\le i<a$ and use the tuple $(a,b_0,\ldots,b_{a-1})$. A configuration consists of $x$ copies of $a$ and a list of occurrences $b_i$. The rules replace $b_0$ by two copies of $a$, replace $b_i+b_j$ by $a+a+b_{i+j}$ when $i+j<a$, and replace it by $b_0+b_0+b_{i+j-a}$ otherwise. Each rule preserves value and raises length by one (`rewrite_value`, `rewrite_size`). Positive generators bound length by value (`size_le_value`). Strong induction on value minus length produces a terminal configuration (`normalizes`).
+
+A terminal list is empty or consists of one positive index. Its residue modulo $a$ determines that index because multiplication by $2$ is cancellable modulo $a$ under coprimality (`cancel_residue`, using `Nat.ModEq.cancel_left_of_coprime`; `terminal_unique`). Induction over the actual rewrite trace supplies every intervening length (`trace_interval`). Coordinate packing and expansion preserve value and length (`pack_value`, `pack_size`, `pack_expand`, `expand_value`, `expand_size`, `lengths_iff`). Thus any length between two represented lengths is represented (`family_intermediate`). At value $2a$, lengths $1$ and $2$ occur, giving global delta set $\{1\}$ (`family_delta`). These helper declarations are private in the settling module.
+
+At $a=3$, `generators_three` identifies $(3,6,8,10)$ with this family. The proof of `result` instantiates the universal assertion at $(a,h,d,k)=(3,2,2,2)$ and contradicts its initial Euclidean coordinate $2\in E(1,2)$.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+The source equality predicts a gap $2$ for $(3,6,8,10)$. Complete interval realization excludes that gap for every represented value; finite-window agreement alone would not suffice. The conclusion concerns the displayed expanded tuple, not the invariant obtained by first deleting redundant generators.
+
+## Evidence
+
+`D5.S3.Arith.Additive.NarayanExpandedGeneratorDeltaRefutation.result` proves the literal negation of `claim`. Its public surface consists of the eight necessary definitions and this single theorem; all auxiliary declarations are private and consumed. It imports Mathlib only and has no D5 frozen prerequisite.
+
+The public result is the designated refutation result (`basis=refutes`) and is exempt from four-slot escape registration (CLAUDE.md §3.9).
+
+### Exact-arithmetic experiment
+
+The checker is [the experiments directory at revision `23c744d471f53c63a530ec05520a55c2902f2050`](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing-experiments/tree/23c744d471f53c63a530ec05520a55c2902f2050/docs/reports/numerical-monoid-delta-set/), file `check.py`. Its SHA-256 is `6e39c9873b672007c385e46c4af6973fd500dbe17f6b37dc47fe46a2da1ab89a`. The implementation seat verified that Git object and reran its exact bytes with `python3 /Users/auric/.sshx/e7c0965424bb6ad207361044/attempt-1/experiment-check.py`, exit 0, final result `ALL_CHECKS_OK`.
+
+The tested scope is 87,175 rewrite identities and residue bijections for odd $a=3,\ldots,101$; 27,803 coordinate factorizations at $a\in\{3,5,7,9,11\}$, $0\le n\le120$; and 74,415 represented values for odd $a=3,\ldots,31$, $0\le n\le5000$. Every tested nonempty family length set is an interval and each observed delta union is $\{1\}$. The checker also gives $E(1,2)=\{1,2\}$ and observes delta union $\{1,2,3,4\}$ for the unexpanded tuple $(3,8,10)$ through $n=2000$. These are finite computations, not the unbounded proof.
+
+## Triage
+
+1. **Proved, kernel-checked:** the binding universal Conjecture 18.3 claim is false, with witness $(3,2,2,2)$ (`result`).
+2. **Proved, kernel-checked:** for every positive $a$ coprime to $2$, all represented family length sets are integer intervals (`family_intermediate`) and the global delta set is $\{1\}$ (`family_delta`). For odd $a\ge3$, the parameters $h=d=2$, $k=a-1$ meet the source restrictions.
+3. **Proved:** value preservation and unit length increments are kernel-checked by `rewrite_value` and `rewrite_size`; terminal reachability is kernel-checked by `normalizes`, and uniqueness by `terminal_unique`. Termination of every rewrite sequence also follows in prose: value stays fixed, length increases by one at every step, and `size_le_value` bounds it above by that value, so an infinite sequence is impossible.
+4. **Computed:** $E(1,2)=\{1,2\}$, with terminating trace $(1,2)\to(1,1)$, by the exact-arithmetic experiment above. The formal refutation uses only initial-state membership $2\in E(1,2)$, constructed directly inside `result`.
+5. **Computed:** the same verified checker validates 87,175 rewrite identities, 27,803 bounded coordinate factorizations and 74,415 represented values, with the exact windows given above and final result `ALL_CHECKS_OK`. These windows are not the unbounded proof.
+6. **Computed:** without the redundant $6$ coordinate, $(3,8,10)$ has observed delta union $\{1,2,3,4\}$ for $0\le n\le2000$, by the same checker. The paper's main theorem for the unexpanded tuple remains a separate assertion.
+7. **Open:** classification for other $h,d,k$, sharpness of the coprimality hypothesis, and catenary Conjectures 18.1 and 18.2 are not settled here.
+
+### What the settlement shows
+
+The failure mechanism is the extra factorization coordinate $ah$: for $h=2$ the family-specific replacements fill all intermediate lengths, while the Euclidean prediction still includes $2$. The positive coprime family above survives as the precise interval and singleton-delta statements proved by the private helpers. The computational assertion about the tuple omitting $ah$ has only the stated finite scope. The refutation supplies no conclusion about the catenary conjectures or the main theorem for unexpanded generators; an application of the expanded equality requires an independent valid replacement. No classification outside this family or sharpness of coprimality is asserted.
+
+### Literature status
+
+The preregistration records the versioned arXiv source and earlier Narayan Zenodo preprints: the expanded equality is still a conjecture in record 22740972, while record 22888273 treats the tuple without $ah$. The screen also covers nonminimal-generator and presentation literature and the searched repository and external formalization scopes. No settlement was located within that recorded scope. Source fidelity and the mathematical proof do not establish worldwide novelty; completeness remains `ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED`.
+
+## ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED
+

+## 8. Diverging surplus ratios and the transition scale
+
+**Definition 8.1 (Scale and error conventions).** In this section $a\ge4$ and $h\ge1$ are integers, $s=a+1+h$, and $M(a,h)$ and $B_0(a)$ retain Definition 1.1. In particular, the infimum is over all laws in $\mathcal X(a,h)$, with arbitrary nonempty cardinalities, zero type masses, arbitrarily small positive actual marginals and possibly disconnected support. Put
+
+$$
+\rho_a=\frac{h}{a^{3/2}}.
+\tag{8.1}
+$$
+
+Every sequential limit below is asserted for every sequence of these integers with $a\to\infty$ and the displayed scale assumptions. For a fixed compact interval $I=[\rho_-,\rho_+]\subset(0,\infty)$, an error $O_I(a^{-1})$ has a constant and a starting value of $a$ depending only on $I$, uniformly over all integers $h$ with $\rho_a\in I$.
+
+**Theorem 8.2 (The surplus between the square-root and transition scales).** For every integer sequence with
+
+$$
+\frac{h}{\sqrt a}\longrightarrow\infty,
+\qquad \frac{h}{a^{3/2}}\longrightarrow0,
+$$
+
+one has
+
+$$
+\frac{M(a,h)-B_0(a)}{a^{3/2}h}\longrightarrow4.
+\tag{8.2}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** Theorem 2.1 is a lower bound for every original law, so
+
+$$
+M(a,h)-B_0(a)
+\ge\beta_a(h+1)-2a^2-a.
+$$
+
+Here $\beta_a/a^{3/2}\to4$, $h\to\infty$ and $\sqrt a/h\to0$. Division by $a^{3/2}h$ gives the lower limit at least $4$.
+
+For a matching upper bound choose
+
+$$
+j=\left\lceil\frac{h}{2\sqrt a}\right\rceil.
+$$
+
+Then $j\to\infty$, $j/a\to0$, $j/h\to0$ and $j\sqrt a/h\to1/2$. In particular $1\le j\le h$ eventually. Use the exact law of Theorem 3.1 at this varying integer $j$, rather than its fixed-$j$ asymptotic formula. Its feasibility for each such integer can also be read directly: with $m=a+j$, $n=h+1-j$ and $p=j/(m-1)$, the core mass $1-p=(a-1)/(m-1)$ and the $n$ singleton masses $p/n$ sum to one, their actual marginals are respectively $1-p>0$ and $p/n>0$, and
+
+$$
+\mathbb E K=(1-p)m+p=m-p(m-1)=a.
+$$
+
+Thus, for every $1\le j\le h$, not just fixed $j$, the unrestricted infimum is at most the exact energy
+
+$$
+H_j(a,h)=\frac{(a+j)^3(a+j-1)}{a-1}
+       +\frac{(h+1-j)^2(a+j-1)}j.
+\tag{8.3}
+$$
+
+For $1\le j\le a/2$, expansion of its first term has a uniform remainder:
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\frac{(a+j)^3(a+j-1)}{a-1}
+ &=a^3+4a^2j+R_{a,j},\\
+R_{a,j}
+ &=\frac{a^2j+3a(2a-1)j^2+(4a-1)j^3+j^4}{a-1}
+ =O(aj^2+aj).
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{8.4}
+$$
+
+The constant is absolute, as follows by bounding $j/a\le1/2$ in the displayed expression. Our choice of $j$ eventually lies in this range. The contribution of $4a^2j$ divided by $a^{3/2}h$ tends to $2$, while the remainder divided by the same quantity is
+
+$$
+O\!\left(\frac{h}{a^{3/2}}+\frac1a\right)=o(1).
+$$
+
+For the other term of (8.3), the exact normalized expression is
+
+$$
+\frac{(h+1-j)^2(a+j-1)}{j a^{3/2}h}
+=\left(\frac{h+1-j}{h}\right)^2
+ \frac{a+j-1}{a}\,\frac{h}{j\sqrt a}
+\longrightarrow2.
+$$
+
+Finally $(B_0(a)-a^3)/(a^{3/2}h)=(2a^2+a)/(a^{3/2}h)\to0$. This actual law gives the upper limit at most $4$, proving (8.2). No law attaining $M$ was used. ∎
+
+**Definition 8.3 (Transition profile).** For $\rho>0$, let $t(\rho)>1$ be the unique solution of
+
+$$
+\rho=2(t-1)t^{3/2},
+\qquad F(\rho)=t(\rho)^4\bigl(4t(\rho)-3\bigr).
+\tag{8.5}
+$$
+
+Uniqueness and existence follow because $t\mapsto2(t-1)t^{3/2}$ is continuous on $(1,\infty)$, has derivative $\sqrt t(5t-3)>0$, and has endpoint limits $0$ and $\infty$.
+
+**Theorem 8.4 (Full-law transition value and uniform first correction).** For every $I=[\rho_-,\rho_+]\subset(0,\infty)$ there are constants $C_I<\infty$ and $A_I$ such that all integers $a\ge A_I$, $h\ge1$ with $\rho_a=h/a^{3/2}\in I$ satisfy
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{M(a,h)}{a^3}-F(\rho_a)
+           +\frac{2\rho_a t(\rho_a)}{\sqrt a}\right|
+\le\frac{C_I}{a}.
+\tag{8.6}
+$$
+
+The profile also has the variational representation
+
+$$
+F(\rho)=\min_{0<p<1}\left\{(1-p)^{-4}+\frac{\rho^2}{p}\right\}.
+\tag{8.7}
+$$
+
+Consequently every integer sequence with $\rho_a\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$ has $M(a,h)/a^3\to F(\rho)$. The normalization in (8.6) uses $h$, with $s=a+1+h$ still exact.

+**Proof.** First, under $t=(1-p)^{-1}$ the objective in (8.7) becomes
+
+$$
+f_\rho(t)=t^4+\rho^2\frac{t}{t-1},\qquad t>1.
+$$
+
+It diverges at both endpoints, and
+
+$$
+f_\rho'(t)=4t^3-\frac{\rho^2}{(t-1)^2},\qquad
+f_\rho''(t)=12t^2+\frac{2\rho^2}{(t-1)^3}>0.
+$$
+
+Its unique minimum is at the solution of (8.5); substitution gives $f_\rho(t)=t^4(4t-3)$. This proves (8.7). The inverse defining $t(\rho)$ is continuous. Thus, for $\rho\in I$, its values lie in an interval $[1+\delta,T]$ with $\delta>0$ and $T<\infty$ depending only on $I$.

+For the full-law lower bound, reuse the pointwise certificate underlying Theorem 2.1 with a movable real contact parameter. The necessary scaled calculation is as follows. For any real $c\ge2$, put
+

+\begin{aligned}

+\tag{8.8}
+$$

+\tag{8.18}

+$$

+T&:=\mathbb E[X^{-1/2};X\ge1],\\
+T-\mathbb E(X+1)^{-1/2}
+&=\mathbb E[X^{-1/2}-(X+1)^{-1/2};X\ge1]-\mathbb P(X=0).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+其中期望的被积项介于 $0$ 与 $1/(2X^{3/2})$ 之间；
+$\mathbb P(X=0)=(1-t)^M\le e^{-\lambda}\le1/\lambda$。
+因此当 $\lambda\ge1$ 时，
+
+$$
+\left|T-\lambda^{-1/2}\right|
+\le\frac2\lambda+\frac{\sqrt3}{\lambda^{3/2}}
+\le\frac4\lambda.
+$$
+
+另由 $\operatorname{Var}X=\lambda(1-t)$，
+
+$$
+\left|\mathbb E\sqrt X-\sqrt\lambda\right|
+\le\mathbb E\frac{|X-\lambda|}{\sqrt\lambda}
+\le1.
+$$
+
+这些都是有限分布的估计，并且保留了 $\mathbb P(X=0)$。
+
+（二）估计导数。令 $Z=1+\operatorname{Bin}(a-1,t)$、$\lambda=at$。
+上述移位恒等式在此给出 $\mathbb EZ^{-1}\le1/\lambda$；又
+$\mathbb EZ=\lambda+1-t$，故
+
+$$
+\mathbb E\frac{(Z-\lambda)^2}{Z}\le1-t\le1,\qquad
+\left|\mathbb EZ^{-1/2}-\lambda^{-1/2}\right|\le\lambda^{-1}.
+$$
+
+为同时处理 $Z=1$，对每个整数 $k\ge1$ 定义
+
+$$
+A(k)=\frac1{1+\sqrt{1-1/k}}.
+$$
+
+若 $s=\sqrt{1-1/k}$，直接有理化给出
+
+$$
+A(k)=\frac12+\frac1{8k}+r_k,\qquad
+r_k=\frac{3+s}{8k^2(1+s)^3},\qquad
+0\le r_k\le\frac3{8k^2},\qquad
+0\le A(k)-\frac12\le\frac1{2k}.
+$$
+
+最后两个界来自 $(3+s)/(1+s)^3\le3$ 和
+$A(k)-1/2=1/(2k(1+s)^2)$。特别地 $A(1)=1$、$r_1=3/8$，没有舍去端点。
+因为 $d_{Z-1}=A(Z)/\sqrt Z$，(7.12) 给出
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+0\le\alpha_a(t)&\le\min\{\sqrt a,t^{-1/2}\},\\
+\left|\alpha_a(t)-\frac1{2\sqrt t}\right|
+&\le\frac{\sqrt a}{2}
+ \left(\lambda^{-1}+\mathbb EZ^{-3/2}\right)
+\le\frac1{\sqrt a\,t}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+第一行使用 $d_r\le1$、$d_{Z-1}\le Z^{-1/2}$ 以及
+$\mathbb EZ^{-1/2}\le(\mathbb EZ^{-1})^{1/2}$；第二行用 $Z\ge1$。
+
+（三）估计度数增量。令 $N=n+1$、$K\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,t)$。
+复用引理 7.3 的条件 Jensen 差：$q_{n,0}=0$，对 $1\le k\le N$，
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+q_{n,k}
+&=\sqrt{\frac kN}
+-\frac{N-k}{N}\sqrt{\frac kn}
+-\frac kN\sqrt{\frac{k-1}{n}}\\
+&=\frac{\sqrt k}{N\sqrt n}\bigl(A(k)-A(N)\bigr).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+因为 $A$ 递减，这也逐项证明非负性；$k=N$ 时恰为零。
+于是有包含全部端点的有限和
+
+$$
+G_n(t)=\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^N
+ \binom Nk t^k(1-t)^{N-k}\sqrt k\bigl(A(k)-A(N)\bigr).
+$$
+
+由 $A(k)-A(N)\le1/(2k)$ 及（一）的第一个逆矩界，
+
+$$
+0\le G_n(t)\le\frac{\sqrt n}{2}\mathbb E[K^{-1/2};K\ge1]
+\le\frac{\sqrt n}{2}\sqrt{\frac2{Nt}}
+\le\frac1{\sqrt{2t}}.
+$$
+
+现在设 $nt\ge1$，令 $\lambda=Nt$、
+$T=\mathbb E[K^{-1/2};K\ge1]$、$U=\mathbb E\sqrt K$。
+使用上面的 $r_k$ 精确分解，
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+G_n(t)&=\frac{\sqrt n}{8}\left(T-\frac UN\right)+R_n(t),\\
+R_n(t)&=\sqrt n\,\mathbb E[\sqrt K(r_K-r_N);K\ge1],\\
+|R_n(t)|
+&\le\frac{3\sqrt n}{8}\mathbb E[K^{-3/2};K\ge1]
+ +\frac{3\sqrt n}{8N^2}\mathbb E\sqrt K\\
+&\le\frac{3\sqrt3}{4nt^{3/2}}+\frac{3\sqrt t}{8n}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+此处 $\sqrt n/N^{3/2}\le1/n$、
+$\sqrt{nN}/N^2\le1/n$，且 Jensen 给 $U\le\sqrt{Nt}$。
+把 $T$ 换成 $\lambda^{-1/2}$ 的误差至多
+$1/(2\sqrt n\,t)$，把 $U$ 换成 $\sqrt\lambda$ 的误差至多
+$1/(8\sqrt n)$。换完后的主项为
+$\sqrt{n/N}(1-t)/(8\sqrt t)$。
+再用 $1-\sqrt{n/N}\le1/(2n)$，得到完整的误差界
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\left|G_n(t)-\frac{1-t}{8\sqrt t}\right|
+&\le\frac1{2\sqrt n\,t}+\frac1{8\sqrt n}
++\frac1{16n\sqrt t}
++\frac{3\sqrt3}{4nt^{3/2}}+\frac{3\sqrt t}{8n}\\
+&\le\left(\frac{17}{16}+\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}\right)
+ \frac1{\sqrt n\,t}
+\le\frac5{2\sqrt n\,t}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+第二行只用 $nt\ge1$、$0<t\le1$、$n\ge1$；
+最后用 $\sqrt3<7/4$。没有未展开的余项。
+
+（四）将积分分成 $[0,1/a]$ 和 $[1/a,1]$。
+在第一段，由（二）和（三）的全域上界，
+
+$$
+0\le\int_0^{1/a}\alpha_a(t)G_n(t)\,dt
+\le\sqrt a\int_0^{1/a}\frac{dt}{\sqrt{2t}}=\sqrt2.
+$$
+
+在第二段，$nt\ge1$，故
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\left|\alpha_a(t)G_n(t)-\frac{1-t}{16t}\right|
+&\le\alpha_a(t)\left|G_n(t)-\frac{1-t}{8\sqrt t}\right|
++\frac{1-t}{8\sqrt t}
+ \left|\alpha_a(t)-\frac1{2\sqrt t}\right|\\
+&\le\frac{21}{8\sqrt a\,t^{3/2}}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+这个上界的积分不超过 $21/4$，而
+
+$$
+\int_{1/a}^1\frac{1-t}{16t}\,dt
+=\frac{L-1+1/a}{16}.
+$$
+
+因此，对全部整数 $n\ge a\ge5$，
+
+$$
+\left|n(n+1)L_{a,n}-\frac L{16}\right|
+\le\sqrt2+\frac{21}{4}+\frac1{16}<7<27.
+\tag{8.4}
+$$
+
+$t=0$ 时 $\alpha_a(0)=\sqrt a$、$g_n(0)=0$；
+$t=1$ 时 $g_n(1)=0$。两端均是原有限多项式的值；
+上述含 $t^{-1/2}$ 的界仅在 $t>0$ 使用，且在零处可积。
+最后将 (8.4) 除以 $n(n+1)$，用 (8.3) 及
+$\sum_{n=a}^{b-1}(n(n+1))^{-1}=\delta$ 得 (8.1)。
+$H>0$ 复用 (7.19)，相对误差则由除以 $\delta L/16$ 得到。∎
+
+**定理 8.2（实际 Shapley 份额的三种参数区间）。** 令 $\vartheta=432/L$。
+对全部整数 $b>a\ge5$，有以下有效的相对误差界。
+
+若 $d=b-a$，则
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{H}{dL/(16a^2)}-1\right|
+\le\vartheta+\frac da.
+$$
+
+若 $s=b/a$，对任意指定实数 $r>1$，则
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{H}{(1-1/r)L/(16a)}-1\right|
+\le\vartheta+(1+\vartheta)\frac{|s-r|}{s(r-1)}.
+$$
+
+同时，
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{H}{L/(16a)}-1\right|
+\le\vartheta+\frac ab.
+$$
+
+因而，分别在 $d=o(a)$、$s\to r\in(1,\infty)$、$s\to\infty$ 时，
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+H&=\frac{dL}{16a^2}\left(1+O(L^{-1}+d/a)\right),\\
+H&=\frac{(1-1/r)L}{16a}
+ \left(1+O_r(L^{-1}+|s-r|)\right),\\
+H&=\frac L{16a}\left(1+O(L^{-1}+a/b)\right).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+第一式、第三式的隐常数绝对；第二式允许依赖固定的 $r$。
+对全部比率共同适用的相对误差仍为 (8.2)。
+
+**证明。** 写 $H=(\delta L/16)(1+\epsilon)$，
+$|\epsilon|\le\vartheta$。第一式的比例因子为 $a/b$，
+故误差不超过 $(a/b)\vartheta+d/b\le\vartheta+d/a$。
+第三式的因子为 $1-a/b$，故误差不超过
+$(1-a/b)\vartheta+a/b\le\vartheta+a/b$。
+第二式使用精确恒等式
+
+$$
+\frac{1-1/s}{1-1/r}-1=\frac{s-r}{s(r-1)}.
+$$
+
+将这个差记为 $v$，则
+$|(1+v)(1+\epsilon)-1|\le\vartheta+(1+\vartheta)|v|$。
+在所述三个极限中相应误差趋于零；第二式不要求对 $r\downarrow1$ 一致。∎
+
+**引理 8.3（连续赤字与合法等删联盟）。** 对 $z,s\in[0,1]$，置
+
+$$
+\mathfrak d_H(z,s)=\sqrt{zs}-\left(\frac12+H\right)z-\left(\frac12-H\right)s .
+$$
+
+则
+
+$$
+\max_{z,s\in[0,1]}\mathfrak d_H(z,s)\le\frac{2H^2}{1+2H},
+\qquad
+D_{a,b}\le\frac{4\sqrt{ab}\,H^2}{1+2H}.
+\tag{8.5}
+$$
+
+令
+
+$$
+ m_a=\max\left\{1,\left\lfloor\frac L4+\frac12\right\rfloor\right\},
+\qquad
+ C_a^\#=(A\setminus K)\sqcup(B\setminus L'),
+\quad |K|=|L'|=m_a .
+$$
+
+则 $C_a^\#$ 是实际合法联盟，并且
+
+$$
+\frac{\Delta(C_a^\#;\phi)}{2\sqrt{ab}}
+ =m_a\delta\left[
+ H-\frac{m_a\delta}
+ {2\bigl(\sqrt{1-m_a/a}+\sqrt{1-m_a/b}\bigr)^2}
+ \right].
+\tag{8.6}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 令 $q=\sqrt{z/s}$（$s=0$ 时直接取值为非正），则
+
+$$
+\mathfrak d_H(z,s)=s\left[q-\left(\frac12+H\right)q^2-\left(\frac12-H\right)\right].
+$$
+
+对固定 $s$，右侧关于 $q$ 的顶点为 $q=(1+2H)^{-1}$，其值为 $2H^2s/(1+2H)$，故 (8.5) 的第一式成立。对实际联盟，(4.9) 给出
+$\Delta/(2\sqrt{ab})=\mathfrak d_H(i/a,j/b)$；取最大值即得第二式。
+
+对 $C_a^\#$ 令 $z=1-m_a/a$、$s=1-m_a/b$。恒等式
+
+$$
+\sqrt{zs}=1-\frac12\left(\frac{m_a}{a}+\frac{m_a}{b}\right)
+-\frac12(\sqrt z-\sqrt s)^2
+$$
+
+和 $z-s=-m_a\delta$ 给出 (8.6)。由 $\log a\le a-1$，
+$m_a\le1+L/4\le(a+3)/4\le a/2$（$a\ge5$），
+所以两个删除集合均为合法的有限标号集合。∎
+
+**定理 8.4（全局有符号赤字渐近）。** 对所有整数 $b>a\ge5$，置
+
+$$
+D_0(a,b)=\frac{(b-a)^2L^2}{64(ab)^{3/2}}
+=\frac{\sqrt{ab}\,\delta^2L^2}{64},
+\qquad
+\mathcal E_D(a)=\frac{10^6}{L}+\frac{10^6L}{a}.
+$$
+
+则
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{D_{a,b}}{D_0(a,b)}-1\right|\le\mathcal E_D(a),
+\tag{8.7}
+$$
+
+其中下界按 $(1-\mathcal E_D)D_0\le D$ 理解；当右端为负时它仍是有效的有限域下界。特别地，误差只依赖于 $a$ 且趋于零，并有统一渐近
+
+$$
+D_{a,b}\sim\frac{(b-a)^2\log(a)^2}{64(ab)^{3/2}}
+\qquad(a\to\infty),
+\tag{8.8}
+$$
+
+量词为所有整数 $b>a$。
+
+**证明。** 先由 (8.5) 和 (8.2) 得
+
+$$
+\frac{D_{a,b}}{D_0(a,b)}
+\le\frac{(1+432/L)^2}{1+2H}
+\le(1+432/L)^2\le1+10^6/L.
+\tag{8.9}
+$$
+
+最后一步可由 $L\ge\log5>1$ 核对：
+$(1+432/L)^2-1=(864+186624/L)/L<10^6/L$。
+这是全体实际联盟的上界。对下界，若 $\mathcal E_D(a)\ge1$，只需使用 $D_{a,b}\ge0$；同时 (8.9) 已给出所需上界。设以下 $\mathcal E_D(a)<1$，于是 $L>10^6$ 且 $L/a<10^{-6}$。令 $m=m_a$，则
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{4m}{L}-1\right|\le\frac2L,
+\qquad
+\left|\frac{16H}{\delta L}-1\right|\le\frac{432}{L},
+\qquad
+\frac ma\le\frac{L+2}{4a}.
+\tag{8.10}
+$$
+
+令 $t=4m/L$、$u=m/a$、$\vartheta=432/L$、
+$S=\sqrt{1-m/a}+\sqrt{1-m/b}$。
+式 (8.6) 及 $S^2\ge4(1-u)$ 直接给出
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\frac{\Delta(C_a^\#;\phi)}{D_0}
+&\ge2t(1-\vartheta)-\frac{t^2}{1-u}\\
+&=1-(t-1)^2-2t\vartheta-\frac{t^2u}{1-u}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+这里 $|t-1|\le2/L$、$t\le2$、
+$u\le(L+2)/(4a)\le L/(2a)<1/2$。因此损失至多
+
+$$
+\frac4{L^2}+\frac{1728}{L}+8u
+\le\frac{1732}{L}+\frac{4L}{a}
+\le10^5\left(\frac1L+\frac La\right).
+$$
+
+这证明了
+
+$$
+\frac{\Delta(C_a^\#;\phi)}{2\sqrt{ab}}
+\ge\frac{\delta^2L^2}{128}
+ \left(1-10^5\left(\frac1L+\frac La\right)\right).
+\tag{8.11}
+$$
+
+乘以 $2\sqrt{ab}$，(8.11) 给出
+$D_{a,b}/D_0\ge1-10^5(1/L+L/a)\ge1-\mathcal E_D(a)$。
+与 (8.9) 合并即得 (8.7)。由于 $\mathcal E_D(a)\to0$ 而不含 $b$，(8.8) 是全局而非固定比率的结论。式 (8.6) 是所要求的物理可实现整数联盟比较；本定理没有断言任何有限 $b$ 的精确最大联盟。
+∎
+
+**定理 8.5（每一个最大联盟的联合计数）。** 设 $C$ 是任意实际最大赤字联盟，记
+
+$$
+ i=a-k,\quad j=b-l,\quad x=\frac ka,\quad y=\frac lb,\quad q=x-y.
+$$
+
+令
+
+$$
+\vartheta(a)=\frac{432}{L},\qquad
+\sigma(a)=\mathcal E_D(a)+2\vartheta(a)+\vartheta(a)^2.
+$$
+
+在 $\sigma(a)<1/4$ 的范围内，所有这样的最大联盟同时满足
+
+$$
+\frac ia\ge1-\frac{4\sigma(a)}{(1-\sqrt{\sigma(a)})^2},
+\qquad
+\frac jb\ge1-\frac{4\sigma(a)}{(1-\sqrt{\sigma(a)})^2}.
+\tag{8.12}
+$$
+
+$$
+\left|q-4H\right|\le4H\sqrt{\sigma(a)}.
+\tag{8.13}
+$$
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{q}{\delta L/4}-1\right|
+\le Q(a):=\frac{432}{L}+(1+\vartheta(a))\sqrt{\sigma(a)}.
+\tag{8.14}
+$$
+
+因此 $i/a,j/b\to1$，并且
+
+$$
+\frac jb-\frac ia\sim4H,
+\qquad
+\frac ka-\frac lb\sim\frac{\delta L}{4}.
+\tag{8.15}
+$$
+
+等价的联合缺失计数关系保留比率因子：
+
+$$
+\left|
+ \frac{k-(a/b)l}{(1-a/b)L/4}-1
+\right|\le Q(a).
+$$
+
+这些式子对所有并列最大联盟同时成立；它们没有分别给出 $k$ 和 $l$ 的无约束比率律。
+
+**证明。** 由 (8.6) 的同一平方根恒等式，对任意 $x,y$ 有
+
+$$
+\frac{\Delta(C;\phi)}{2\sqrt{ab}}
+=Hq-\frac12(\sqrt{1-x}-\sqrt{1-y})^2.
+\tag{8.16}
+$$
+
+由 (7.19)、(7.23)，最大赤字严格为正，故 (8.16) 蕴含 $q>0$。
+因此 $S=\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1-y}>0$，则第二项为 $q^2/(2S^2)$，且 $S^2\le4$。所以
+
+$$
+2H^2-\mathfrak d_H(1-x,1-y)
+\ge\frac{(q-4H)^2}{8}.
+\tag{8.17}
+$$
+
+此外 $4-S^2\ge x+y$、$S^2\le4$，故
+
+$$
+2H^2-\mathfrak d_H(1-x,1-y)
+\ge\frac{(q-4H)^2}{8}+\frac{q^2(x+y)}{32}.
+\tag{8.18}
+$$
+
+由 (8.7)、(8.2)，最大联盟的归一化赤字至少为
+$2H^2(1-\sigma(a))$；这里使用
+$(1-\mathcal E_D)/(1+\vartheta)^2\ge1-\sigma$。于是 (8.17) 给出 (8.13)，并给出
+$q\ge4H(1-\sqrt\sigma)$。再代入 (8.18)，得到
+$x+y\le4\sigma/(1-\sqrt\sigma)^2$，即 (8.12)。最后
+
+$$
+|q-\delta L/4|\le|q-4H|+4|H-\delta L/16|
+\le4H\sqrt\sigma+108\delta,
+$$
+
+再用 $16H/(\delta L)\le1+\vartheta$，即得 (8.14)。因为 $\mathcal E_D(a),\vartheta(a)\to0$，(8.15) 随即成立。∎
+
+**推论 8.6（固定差值的等删计数）。** 固定正整数 $d$，令 $b=a+d$。若 $a$ 满足
+
+$$
+L\ge8,\quad a\ge10^6L^3,\quad
+\sigma(a)<\frac1{16},\quad
+d\,\frac{L/2+216}{a+d}<1,\quad
+ d\,\frac{4\sigma(a)}{(1-\sqrt{\sigma(a)})^2}<1,
+\tag{8.19}
+$$
+
+则每一个实际最大赤字联盟都有
+
+$$
+ k=l=m,\qquad
+\left|m-\frac L4\right|\le300.
+\tag{8.20}
+$$
+
+条件 (8.19) 对每个固定 $d$ 由足够大的 $a$ 满足，因此
+$k=l=L/4+O(1)$，其中误差界 $300$ 与 $d$、$a$ 无关。
+
+**证明。** 最大联盟的赤字为正，故由 (8.16) 有 $0<q<8H$。由 (8.1)，
+
+$$
+q<\delta\left(\frac L2+216\right).
+\tag{8.21}
+$$
+
+若 $k-l\ge1$，则
+$q=(k-l)/a+ld/(ab)\ge1/a$，与 (8.19)、(8.21) 矛盾。若 $l-k\ge1$，则 $q>0$ 要求 $ld/b>1$；而 (8.12) 和 (8.19) 给出 $l/b\le x+y<1/d$，也矛盾。故 $k=l=m$。
+
+在等删情形，$q=m\delta$。记
+$h=H/\delta=L/16+e$、$|e|\le27$，并令
+$M=4h=L/4+4e$、$P(r)=rh-r^2/8$。
+对实际最大联盟 $C_m$，由 $S^2\le4$ 得
+
+$$
+\frac{\Delta(C_m;\phi)}{2\sqrt{ab}\,\delta^2}\le P(m).
+\tag{8.22}
+$$
+
+取 $m_0$ 为最接近 $L/4$ 的正整数；$L\ge8$ 保证
+$|m_0-L/4|\le1/2$，且 $m_0$ 合法。由
+$S^2\ge4(1-m_0/a)$ 得
+
+$$
+\frac{\Delta(C_{m_0};\phi)}{2\sqrt{ab}\,\delta^2}
+\ge P(m_0)-\frac{m_0^3}{8a(1-m_0/a)}.
+\tag{8.23}
+$$
+
+由 $m_0\le L/4+1/2\le5L/16$、
+$a\ge10^6L^3$，有 $m_0/a<1/2$，且最后的修正项至多
+$125L^3/(16384a)<1$。
+配方 $P(r)=2h^2-(r-M)^2/8$，
+以及 $|M-L/4|\le108$，给出
+$|m_0-M|\le108+1/2$。
+若 $|m-L/4|>300$，则 $|m-M|>192$，于是
+
+$$
+P(m)-P(m_0)
+<-\frac{192^2-(108+1/2)^2}{8}<-3000.
+$$

+这个步骤只解析延拓截断的低频积分。
+
+对实际高频积分只在实轴逐次求导，使用 (129.3)。对 $k\le p$，
+
+$$
+\int_{|\xi|>T}(1+|\xi|)^{2k}E_Q(\xi)\,d\xi
+ \le \exp\{-c/\delta+C(k+1)\log[Q(k+2)]\}.
+\tag{129.12}
+$$
+
+为核对范围，在 $T<|\xi|\le\delta^{-1/2}$ 上
+$E_Q\le e^{-c_1\xi^2}$，其带幂尾积分至多
+$e^{-c_2/\delta}C^{k+1}\delta^{-k-1}$，因为
+$k\log(k+2)=o(1/\delta)$。
+外侧置 $v=\sqrt\delta|\xi|\ge1$，把
+$(1+cv^2)^{-c'/\delta}$ 的一半保留为 $e^{-c_3/\delta}$，另一半积分
+$v^{2k}(1+cv^2)^{-c'/(2\delta)}$；$2k+2<c'/(4\delta)$ 最终成立。
+该积分至多 $C^{k+1}$，另有尺度因子 $\delta^{-k-1}$。
+这证明 (129.12)，也证明每一实际导数的反演与积分交换合法。
+合并低频与高频即得 (129.4)。
+
+为证明 (129.6)，在同一倾斜 Fourier 积分中插入多项式。
+频率 $u$ 下坐标的复均值、协方差正是 (125.3)，其模不超过 $|m_j|,w_j$。
+$\mathcal D_G$ 的复均值和协方差的模至多 $C\delta^3,C$。
+复 Gaussian 的 $2k$ 次矩公式含至多 $(2k)!$ 个配对项，因而该插入的模至多
+$[C(k+1)]^{2k}$ 倍 $|\psi|$。
+对 $S_G^k$ 展开有序的 $k$ 个坐标指标；
+$w_j/v_j\le C$、$e_j^2/v_j\le Ce_M^2$ 使其配对和至多
+$[C(k+1)]^{2k}(1+m_Q)^k|\psi|$。
+这些估计也覆盖非常小但为正的 $v_j$。
+
+能量噪声在倾斜下的均值是 $t_\alpha\delta\sigma^2/\alpha$、方差是
+$\delta\sigma^2/\alpha$；再作 Fourier 插入并除以 $\sqrt\delta\sigma$，
+复均值的模至多 $C(\sigma/\sqrt\delta+|\xi|\sigma)$、复方差的模至多 $C$。
+条件于总能量等于 $V+\sqrt\delta y$ 时，它的负值正是 $U_y$。
+因此 $U_y^{2k}$ 的插入至多
+$[C(k+1)]^{2k}\delta^{-k}(1+|\xi|)^{2k}|\psi|$。
+没有使用 $\sigma^{-2k}$ 来界这个条件插入。
+全频积分的相应矩至多 $[C(k+1)]^{C(k+1)}$：低频用 Gaussian 矩，
+高频用 (129.12)。分母 $q_\alpha(z_y)\ge c_R$ 由 (129.4) 的零阶部分给出。
+这证明 $s=0$ 的 (129.6)。
+
+由精确公式 (125.8)，$\mathcal J_\eta/\mathcal J_0=1+O(\eta)$；
+分子是同一个条件 Fourier 积分，并由 (129.9) 控制。
+带选择的非负多项式分子不超过无选择的分子，而分母至少保留一半，
+故 (129.6) 对 $s=\eta$ 也成立。
+
+在截断 Taylor 代数中，(128.2) 的加权系数和次乘性成立。
+$\varphi(z_y)$ 及其倒数在共同系数圆盘上有 $C_R$ 上界，
+故它们的 $\rho$ 系数和也有此界。
+(129.4) 使 $q_\alpha(z_y)/\varphi(z_y)-1$ 的 $p$ 喷射范数趋零；
+对 $\log(1+v)$ 和 $(1+v)^{-1}$ 使用绝对收敛幂级数即可控制对数与倒数喷射。
+同理，对 (125.8) 的分子使用 (129.9)、(129.11)–(129.12)，再乘这个倒数喷射，
+得到 (129.5)。这个代数论证只需有限阶真实导数和实点正密度。
+
+最后，若 $\sigma'^2/\sigma^2=1+\omega$ 且 $|\omega|$ 为所列指数小量，
+在同一个 $t_\alpha$ 处，$K_H,K'_H,W_H$ 的精确变化由 (126.6) 给出。
+其系数加权和至多 $\operatorname{poly}(Q)|\omega|$。
+新的标准化输出位置仍在原固定紧集，新的密度仍有正下界，
+反倾斜前因子的对数变化也是 $\operatorname{poly}(Q)|\omega|$。
+所以邻近宽度的核积分之比有固定上下界，上述插入界不变。∎
+
+**推论 129.3（完整有限根的 Gaussian 响应喷射）。** 对原 $g_\alpha$，有
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+N_p\left(\log\frac{g_\alpha(y)}{g_\alpha(0)}
+       +\sqrt\delta t_\alpha y+\frac{\delta y^2}{2W_\alpha}\right)
+&\le C\sqrt\delta+
+ e^{-c/\delta+C(p+1)\log[Q(p+2)]}\\
+&\quad+e^{-\mu Q^3/64+C(p+1)\log[Q(p+2)]}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{129.13}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 用原精确撤倾斜公式 (123.15)，其比值等于
+$e^{-\sqrt\delta t_\alpha y}q_\alpha(z_y)/q_\alpha(z_0)$。
+引理 129.2 的有限 Taylor 对数给
+
+$$
+\log\frac{q_\alpha(z_y)}{q_\alpha(z_0)}
+=-\frac{z_y^2-z_0^2}{2}+r_\alpha(y),
+\qquad N_p(r)\le C\sqrt\delta+e^{-c/\delta+C(p+1)\log[Q(p+2)]}.
+$$
+
+又
+$z_y^2-z_0^2=\delta y^2/W_H+2\sqrt\delta y\epsilon_H/W_H$。
+引理 129.1 支付 $W_H^{-1}-W^{-1}$ 和 $\epsilon_H/W_H$ 的全系数和。
+这给 (129.13)，系数仍为完整 $t,W$。∎
+
+## 130. 全复圆盘上的原计数比较与低于一的同输出 escort
+
+**引理 130.1（全元组、双尾部的复配分比较）。** 取原 $S_Q,\mathcal D,\ell,c_0,\eta$，
+并对 $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ 定义
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+G_y(z)&=J_P(z,y),\\
+\mathcal C_s(z,y)&=B^{|H|}Z_L(z)\mathcal J_s(z,y),
+ &s&\in\{0,\eta\},\\
+\mathcal C_P(z,y)&=e^{zc_0}\mathcal C_\eta(z,y).
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{130.1}
+$$
+
+其中 $Z_L(z)=\sum_{m_{H^c}}e^{-zS_{H^c}(m)}$ 精确保留每个原低元组。
+存在固定 $c,C>0$，使对每个 $a\in[1,2]$，在整个闭圆盘 $|z-a|\le h$ 上，
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+&\frac{|J_s^{\rm count}(z,y)-\mathcal C_s(z,y)|}{\mathcal C_s(a,y)}
+ +\frac{|G_y(z)-\mathcal C_P(z,y)|}{\mathcal C_P(a,y)}\\
+&\hspace{15mm}\le \mathcal E_Q:=
+ \exp\{-\mu Q^3/64+CQ^2\}
+ +\exp\{-cQ^4+L+CQ^2\},\qquad |y|\le R.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{130.2}
+$$
+
+分母均在实点 $a$ 取值；并未在复点除以可能为零的配分函数。
+
+**证明。** 先列出实比较分母及低组的共同界。对实 $b$ 在
+$[1-2h,2+2h]$，(128.7) 给
+
+$$
+\frac{Z_L(b)}{Z_L(a)}\le e^{Cm_Q},\qquad a\in[1,2].
+\tag{130.3}
+$$
+
+它只是每个低组的 $U/D_*$ 比值相乘。若需把 $b>2$ 作为实基点，
+Jensen 在参数 $2$ 及 (128.7) 的 $k=1$ 给
+$Z_j(b)/Z_j(2)=\mathbb E_{2,j}e^{-(b-2)S_j}\ge e^{-(b-2)K(1)}$。
+$b<1$ 时用单调性 $Z_j(b)\ge Z_j(1)$。
+因此所有实基点在所列扩展区间也有同样共同常数的单组上下界。
+对固定自然数 $k$，从 $b-1/2\ge1/4$ 与
+$x^ke^{-x/4}\le[4(k+1)]^k$ 得该扩展区间上的单组惊讶矩界；
+独立低组乘积的第 $k$ 矩至多 $[C(k+1)]^{C(k+1)}(1+m_Q)^k$。
+这是对 (128.7) 的直接使用，不把低组改为 Gaussian。
+
+令 $n_H=|H|$，$Z_H^G(b)=\prod_{H}\sqrt{2\pi v_j/b}$。
+把 Gaussian 积分除以这个无输出常数，(123.15)、(129.4)、(129.5) 给
+
+$$
+c_R\sigma e^{-C_R/\delta}\le
+ \frac{\mathcal J_s(b,y)}{Z_H^G(b)}
+ \le C_R\sigma e^{C_R/\delta},\qquad s\in\{0,\eta\}.
+\tag{130.4}
+$$
+
+这里核积分与概率密度相差精确因子 $\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma/\sqrt b$，
+而 $|K_H(t_b)-t_b(V+\sqrt\delta y)|\le C_R/\delta$，
+$\sqrt\delta/\sqrt{W_H}\asymp1$。所以同输出核在两个实阶数之比满足
+
+$$
+\frac{\mathcal C_s(b,y)}{\mathcal C_s(a,y)}\le e^{CQ^2},
+\qquad |b-a|\le2h,
+\tag{130.5}
+$$
+
+因为 $Z_H^G(b)/Z_H^G(a)=(a/b)^{n_H/2}$，$m_Q\le CQ^2$。
+(130.4) 中的 $\sigma$ 在此精确抵消。
+
+现在取高组中心盒的全部格元。原 (126.3)–(126.4) 对每个接上的原低元组给
+
+$$
+\begin{gathered}
+|S_H-S_G|\le\epsilon_Q\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-\chi Q^3/2},\\
+|T_x-T_G|/\sigma\le\eta_Q
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)
+ \{e^{-(c_q/2-l)Q^3}+e^{-(c_q-2\chi-l)Q^3}\},\\
+|\mathcal D-\mathcal D_G|\le d_Q
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-(c_q/2-\chi)Q^3}.
+\end{gathered}
+\tag{130.6}
+$$
+
+中心盒内 $|\mathcal D_G|\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)$，故
+$|s\mathcal D^2-s\mathcal D_G^2|\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)d_Q$。
+这些都是逐元组界，未删去任何总偏差或低组情形。
+
+写 $b=\operatorname{Re}z$、$U=(T_G-y)/\sigma$。
+对任意两个实势能 $A,B$，基本积分恒等式
+
+$$
+e^{-zA}-e^{-zB}=-z(A-B)\int_0^1e^{-z[(1-v)B+vA]}\,dv
+\tag{130.7}
+$$
+
+使 $|z|\le3$ 的整个圆盘受到同一实 $b$ 的支配。
+(130.6) 和 $|\lambda_y-U^2/2|\le\eta_Q|U|+\eta_Q^2/2$ 给中心格元误差至多
+
+$$
+C(\epsilon_Q+\operatorname{poly}(Q)d_Q+\eta_Q)
+ (1+|U|)e^{C\eta_Q|U|}
+ e^{-b(S_G+S_L+U^2/2+s\mathcal D_G^2)}.
+\tag{130.8}
+$$
+
+系数中的额外固定多项式一并吸收入 $\operatorname{poly}(Q)$。
+用 $C\eta_Q|U|\le \eta_QU^2+C^2\eta_Q/4$ 把线性指数吸收进
+相对变化 $O(\eta_Q)$ 的邻近宽度。引理 129.2 的同输出插入与邻近宽度结论
+使 (130.8) 的总积分至多
+$\operatorname{poly}(Q)(\epsilon_Q+d_Q+\eta_Q)\mathcal C_s(b,y)$。
+格元体积恰为 $B^{-n_H}$；$e^{-zS_L}$ 未改变，
+其复模求和恰为 $Z_L(b)$。除以 $\mathcal C_s(a,y)$ 时只用 (130.5)，
+不再付 $\sigma^{-1}$。这证明整个复圆盘上的中心部分。
+
+还要包括全部离散尾部与全部连续尾部。对 $b\ge1-2h$，
+复核的模不超过一，秩一选择因子的模也不超过一。
+原有限二项的 Gaussian 惊讶包络与半 escort 界 (128.7)，以及原正态尾，分别给
+
+$$
+\mathbb P_{b,H}^{\rm bin}\{\text{高组中心盒外}\}
+ +\mathbb P_{b,H}^{G}\{\text{中心格元并集外}\}
+ \le e^{-cQ^4+Cm_Q}.
+\tag{130.9}
+$$
+
+具体地，对某个坏坐标先从 $e^{-bS_j}$ 留出固定正比例，
+$S_j\ge cz_j^2-C$ 在 $|z_j|>Q^2$ 给 $e^{-cQ^4}$；
+剩余配分由 $Z_j(1/2)$ 支付，分母由 $D_*\sqrt{C_j+1}$ 支付。
+对至多 $CQ^2$ 个坐标求并。Gaussian 同样留出一半二次势能，
+格元边界相差 $O(C_j^{-1/2})$，阈值最终至少 $Q^2/2$，所以仍有该尾指数。
+所有有限端点都在离散尾部内。
+无输出高二项常数与 $B^{n_H}Z_H^G(b)$ 的比由同一中心格元估计及这两个尾部趋于一；
+此处无需输出分母。
+
+于是两种完整尾部在除以 (130.4) 的实际比较分母后，至多
+
+$$
+\exp\{-cQ^4+L+CQ^2\}.
+\tag{130.10}
+$$
+
+这里只用一次 $\sigma^{-1}=e^L$。没有在尾部对似然求导，也没有引入
+$\sigma^{-2k}$。对全部复点同时成立的零阶 raw 估计将承担后面的所有导数。
+由 (130.6)、$\log q=c_qQ^3+O(1)$ 和 (128.1)，中心部分可放宽为
+$e^{-\mu Q^3/64+CQ^2}$。这证明 $J_s^{\rm count}$ 的 (130.2)。
+
+为了回接完整选择，先记录固定电荷插入的比较。在上述同一中心格元插入
+$1+|\mathcal D|^6$，逐元组误差用 (130.6)；Gaussian 条件矩用 (129.6) 的 $k=3$。
+离散全盒有 $|\mathcal D|\le CB$，故插入的最大成本为 $e^{CQ^3}$；
+它被 (130.9) 的 $Q^4$ 指数吸收。连续尾部用 Cauchy–Schwarz 与
+无输出 $\mathcal D_G$ 的第十二矩，其上界为常数。
+所以在实 $b\in[1-h,2+h]$ 的原计数同输出律中，
+
+$$
+\frac{\sum_m(1+|\mathcal D(m)|^6)e^{-bA_y(m)}}{J_0^{\rm count}(b,y)}\le C.
+\tag{130.11}
+$$
+
+实基点区间的小扩展使用 (130.3) 后说明的单组上下界，中心与双尾部证明完全相同。
+即便 $\sigma$ 最慢趋零，该插入的 Gaussian 证明也没有逆噪声成本。
+
+最后使用原全盒二次选择估计 (124.2)。由于
+$\ell,\ell_2\le C\delta^5$，对 $b=\operatorname{Re}z\ge1-h$，(130.7) 给
+
+$$
+|e^{z\ell(m)}-e^{z\ell_2(m)}|
+ \le C|\ell(m)-\ell_2(m)|
+ \le Cq^{-1/2}(1+|\mathcal D(m)|^3).
+\tag{130.12}
+$$
+
+这个不等式在整个原盒成立；两种选择势在极端元组可有很大的负值，
+仍不影响上界。乘 $e^{-bA_y}$ 并用 (130.11)，有
+
+$$
+|G_y(z)-e^{zc_0}J_\eta^{\rm count}(z,y)|
+ \le Cq^{-1/2}J_0^{\rm count}(b,y).
+\tag{130.13}
+$$
+
+$J_0^{\rm count}(b,y)/\mathcal C_P(a,y)\le e^{CQ^2}$ 由已证实 raw 比较、
+(130.5) 及 (129.5) 的零阶部分给出。
+合并 (130.13) 和 $s=\eta$ 的全圆盘比较，即得第二条 (130.2)。
+原全部多重度、全低组幂及完整选择因此都在 raw 估计中。∎

+**引理 130.2（低于一的实际同输出 escort 比）。** 对同一个 $G_y$，有

+\log\frac{G_y(a-h)}{G_y(a)}\le CQ^2,
+\qquad a\in[1,2],\ |y|\le R.
+\tag{130.14}

+**证明。** 先对 Gaussian 比较使用 (130.3)–(130.5)。低组精确成本为
+$(U/D_*)^{|H^c|}$，高组体积归一化成本为 $(a/(a-h))^{n_H/2}$；

+相乘给 (130.14)。其它配分函数相同。
+这不是以无输出半 escort 的比代替同输出比；核积分及选择项已逐项支付。∎

+## 131. 从复 raw 误差到绝对信息累积量
+
+**引理 131.1（实际配分的定量对数转移）。** 对 $p=p(Q)$，
+
+$$
+N_p\left(\log\frac{G_y(\alpha)}{\mathcal C_P(\alpha,y)}\right)
+ \le \exp\{-\mu Q^3/64+CQ^2+C(p+1)\log[Q(p+2)]\}
+ +\exp\{-cQ^4+L+CQ^2+C(p+1)\log[Q(p+2)]\}.
+\tag{131.1}
+$$
+
+$s=0,\eta$ 的计数/比较配分之对数有同一界。
+
+**证明。** 先说明由 (130.14) 产生的零点控制尺度。
+选择 $b_0=C\delta^5$ 大于 $\sup_m\ell(m)$ 及 $c_0$，并令
+
+$$
+\widehat G_y(z)=e^{-zb_0}G_y(z),\qquad
+\widehat C_y(z)=e^{-zb_0}\mathcal C_P(z,y).
+\tag{131.2}
+$$
+
+第一函数是有限个 $e^{-zH_m}$ 的和，其中
+$H_m=A_y+b_0-\ell(m)\ge0$；第二函数是相同类型的正测度积分，
+势能为 $S_L+S_G+\lambda_y^G+\eta\mathcal D_G^2+b_0-c_0\ge0$。
+其有限正实点积分与一阶矩均存在。
+对两者中任一个 $Z$，置 $f(b)=\log Z(b)$。
+对数配分的凸性与单调性，加上 (130.14)，给
+
+$$
+0\le -f'(b)=\mathbb E_bH\le CQ^2,
+\qquad a-h/2\le b\le a.
+\tag{131.3}
+$$
+
+具体地，令 $r=h/2$。由 $H\ge0$，$Z$ 随实参数递减；于是
+$b-r\ge a-h$、$b\le a$ 蕴含
+
+$$
+\mathbb E_b e^{rH}=\frac{Z(b-r)}{Z(b)}
+ \le\frac{Z(a-h)}{Z(a)}\le e^{CQ^2}.
+$$
+
+Jensen 不等式给 $r\mathbb E_bH\le CQ^2$；乘 $e^{-zb_0}$ 的变化仅为
+$O(h\delta^5)$。沿 $[a-h/2,a]$ 积分 (131.3)，对 $0\le r\le h/2$ 有
+
+$$
+\frac{Z(a-r)}{Z(a)}\le e^{CQ^2r}.
+$$
+若 $|z-a|\le r$，正势能的积分表示又给
+
+$$
+\frac{|Z(z)-Z(a)|}{Z(a)}
+ \le\mathbb E_a(e^{rH}-1)
+ =\frac{Z(a-r)}{Z(a)}-1
+ \le e^{CQ^2r}-1.
+\tag{131.4}
+$$
+
+取固定小 $d>0$ 及 $r_Q=dQ^{-2}$，右侧至多 $1/4$。
+于是 $\widehat G_y,\widehat C_y$ 在 $|z-a|\le r_Q$ 上均非零，
+并且 $|\mathcal C_P(z,y)|\ge\mathcal C_P(a,y)/2$。
+这里只得到随 $Q$ 缩小的圆盘，不要求实际配分在固定复条带非零。
+
+由整个固定圆盘上的 (130.2)，在这个小圆盘上有
+
+$$
+\left|\frac{G_y(z)}{\mathcal C_P(z,y)}-1\right|\le2\mathcal E_Q.
+\tag{131.5}
+$$
+

+presentations, finite transients, and the zero stream; it does not
+assume a nonzero constant coefficient or an invertible transition.

+with seed $s_d(P)$ evaluated at the next $d$ positions. A passing row
+therefore generates a member of $\mathscr R_d$ agreeing with the
+authentic stream in its first $2d$ values. GPO Lemma 29.2 makes the two

+Hankel equations. If an annihilator $p$ is divided by the monic $m_P$,
+the remainder also annihilates the stream; minimality forces the
+remainder to vanish. This proves (ACR.79), including the cases in which
+$m_P$ has zero constant coefficient.

+The reductions have polynomial local overhead in $d$ besides their one
+call to the other row/descriptor task; that call retains its own costs,
+including the original enumeration when used. The following local model
+makes the overhead executable without a fixed address-width assumption.

+indices, counters, markers and control, counts cumulatively; reusable
+backing counts every visited tape cell, including blank cells traversed.

+across a string costs its actual scans. Allocation and actual physical
+writes retain their separate tariffs.

+an $M$-bit local array can be implemented by scanning from its left
+marker with a binary position counter, then returning the head. With
+$\ell$ bits sufficient for its positions and loop indices, this costs

+index description, initialization and return scans are included. This

+unit-cost array access.

Thus $\partial_cQ_t(y)=\partial_cQ_t(\mathbf1)=\gamma$, independent of $c$. For $d\notin L$, the endpoint terms of the binomial expansion have rank two and the other terms rank three. Odd $\ell$ cancel, the term $\ell=1$ is zero, and even $\ell\ge2$ give
+
+$$
+\beta=
+\sum_{\substack{2\le\ell\le t-1\\\ell\ \mathrm{even}}}
+\frac{2(t)_{\ell+1}}{\ell!}
+\left(A_{3,t-\ell-1}-A_{2,t-\ell-1}\right)>0.
+$$
+
+Nonnegativity follows from nested subspaces. The $\ell=2$ term is strictly positive: fix nested subspaces $U_2<U_3$ of dimensions two and three, choose a basis of a complement $D$ to $U_3$, and pad its $k-3$ rays to $t-3$ letters with a ray in $U_2$. The resulting word completes $U_3$, whereas its span with $U_2$ is contained in the proper hyperplane $D+U_2$. For $k=3,t=3$ this is the empty word; for $k=3,t>3$ all padding is still inside $U_2$. This verifies $\beta>0$.
+
+Finally choose any $d\notin L$. The vectors $y$ and $y'=\mathbf1-e_a+e_d$ have equal $Q_t$ values by an invertible linear map fixing $a$ and carrying $b$ to $d$. They are distinct positive vectors on $A$ with the same total mass. Applying (16.2) to $y'$ gives $\nabla Q_t(y)\cdot(y'-y)>0$, since the root-to-polynomial gradient factor is positive. Thus $\partial_dQ_t(y)>\partial_bQ_t(y)$, namely $\alpha>\beta$. This completes (16.3).
+
+We now give the integer incidence argument. Let $n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^P$, $\sum_p n_p=N$, $n\ne\mathbf1$, and put $h=n-\mathbf1$. Its negative entries are exactly $-1$. Let $Z=\{p:h_p=-1\}$, $B=\{p:h_p>0\}$, and $z=|Z|=\sum_{b\in B}h_b>0$. For a projective line $L$ put
+
+$$
+Z_L=|Z\cap L|,\qquad B_L=\sum_{b\in B\cap L}h_b,
+\qquad h(L)=B_L-Z_L.
+$$
+
+There exist a line $L$ meeting both $Z$ and $B$, and $b\in B\cap L$, such that
+
+$$
+h(L)\le h_b-1. \tag{16.4}
+$$
+
+Otherwise, integrality would imply $B_L-Z_L\ge M_L:=\max_{b\in B\cap L}h_b$ on every mixed line. On each such line,
+
+$$
+B_LZ_L\le B_L^2-B_LM_L
+\le B_L^2-\sum_{b\in B\cap L}h_b^2.
+$$
+
+The same inequality holds on nonmixed lines because its left side is zero and its right side is the sum of the nonnegative products of distinct positive entries on that line. Each distinct pair of projective points determines exactly one line. Summing over all lines would therefore give
+
+$$
+z^2=\sum_L B_LZ_L
+\le\sum_L\left(B_L^2-\sum_{b\in B\cap L}h_b^2\right)
+=z^2-\sum_{b\in B}h_b^2<z^2,
+$$
+
+a contradiction. Choose $b$ realizing the maximum on a line for which the assumed inequality fails; this proves (16.4). Choose any $a\in Z\cap L$. Then $L=a+b$, $n_a=0$, and $h_b\ge1$.
+
+Use this pair to set $y=\mathbf1-e_a+e_b$. Since $\sum h_p=0$, the gradient values (16.3) give
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\nabla Q_t(y)\cdot(n-y)
+&=-\alpha(h_b-1)-\beta\sum_{p\notin L}h_p\\
+&=-\alpha(h_b-1)+\beta h(L)\\
+&\le-(\alpha-\beta)(h_b-1)\le0.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+The gradient of $\Phi$ has the same positive scalar factor at $y$. If $n\ne y$, (16.2) implies $Q_t(n)<Q_t(y)$. If $n=y$, equality holds. This proves the sharp bound for every nonuniform nonnegative integer multiplicity vector of total $N$, without a restriction on the number or arrangement of its missing and repeated rays. For a zero-free matrix, the exact physical fiber identity gives $R_G(t)=N^{-t}Q_t(n(G))$, and Theorem 15.2 supplies the asserted value and equality characterization.
+
+It remains to treat original zero columns strictly. Suppose $z(G)>0$, choose an original nonzero column on ray $b$, and replace every zero column by that same nonzero vector on its original label. Call the resulting matrix $G'$. Its span contains that of $G$, so it has rank $k$, and every original sampled prefix span is contained in the corresponding new one. Its ray $b$ has multiplicity at least two, so $n(G')\ne\mathbf1$ and the integer comparison applies.
+
+Moreover the probability comparison is strict at every $t\ge k$. Extend the chosen original nonzero column to a basis using original nonzero columns, and retain the other $k-1$ basis labels. A physical word consisting of one original zero label and these $k-1$ labels, padded to length $t$ by one of the retained labels, has probability $N^{-t}>0$. It spans in $G'$ and has rank $k-1$ in $G$. Hence
+
+$$
+R_G(t)<R_{G'}(t)\le S_t-D_t.
+$$
+
+This coupling retains the iid uniform law on all original labels; no zero is removed or conditioned away. Finally fewer than $k$ columns cannot span $V$, which proves the statement for $t<k$. Theorem 15.2 exhibits rank-$k$ equality matrices for every allowed $K,k$, completing attainment and the entire equivalence. $\square$

+## 17. Complete labelled equality assignments
+
+**Theorem 17.1 (representatives, fixed labels, and optional permutations).** Under the field and dimension hypotheses of Theorem 16.1, every original labelled equality matrix, and only such a matrix, is obtained by the following data: an ordered pair of distinct rays $(a,b)$, an unordered two-element subset $J\subset I$, a bijection
+
+$$
+\sigma:I\setminus J\longrightarrow P\setminus\{a,b\},
+$$
+
+and an arbitrary nonzero representative of $b$ at each label in $J$ and of $\sigma(i)$ at each $i\notin J$. Equivalently, after fixing representatives $v_p\in p\setminus\{0\}$, all such matrices have
+
+$$
+G_i=\begin{cases}\lambda_i v_b,&i\in J,\\
+\lambda_i v_{\sigma(i)},&i\notin J,
+\end{cases}
+\qquad \lambda_i\in K^\times.
+$$
+
+With labels fixed, quotienting by invertible row transformations and independent nonzero column scalings is exactly the $\operatorname{PGL}(k,q)$ action on these labelled ray maps $\rho:I\to P$. There is no field-automorphism quotient. If column permutations are additionally allowed, there is exactly one equality type. The raw number of labelled matrices attaining equality, before any of these quotients, is
+
+$$
+N(N-1)\frac{N!}{2}(q-1)^N.
+$$
+
+**Proof.** Theorem 16.1 forces a unique missing ray $a$ and a unique doubled ray $b$. The labels on $b$ form the unique unordered pair $J$, and every remaining label is assigned once to every other ray. This gives precisely $\sigma$ and all its stated data. Conversely every such assignment has exactly the required multiplicities and is zero-free, has rank $k$ by Theorem 15.2, and attains equality at every $t\ge k$. Once the reference $v_p$ are fixed, each nonzero column has one and only one scalar $\lambda_i\in K^\times$, so this parameterization has no further identifications.
+
+Suppose $G'_i=c_i A G_i$ for every fixed label $i$, with $A\in\operatorname{GL}(k,q)$ and $c_i\in K^\times$. Then $\rho'(i)=A\rho(i)$ at each label. Conversely, if this equality of ray maps holds for one $A$, the two nonzero vectors $G'_i$ and $AG_i$ differ by a nonzero scalar $c_i$ separately at each label. Scalar row matrices act trivially on every ray, and quotienting $\operatorname{GL}(k,q)$ by those matrices is precisely $\operatorname{PGL}(k,q)$. To check the action's projective kernel, a linear map fixing every ray fixes basis rays, hence is diagonal, and fixing the rays of sums of two basis vectors forces all diagonal entries equal. This is a linear action over the fixed field $K$; no semilinear transformations are included. Thus the fixed-label classes are exactly the stated projective-group orbits of labelled maps. In particular the double-label pair is preserved by this equivalence, so the optional permutation quotient is a separate operation.
+
+For that optional quotient, $\operatorname{GL}(k,q)$ is transitive on ordered distinct ray pairs: choose independent representatives of each pair, extend each to a basis, and map bases. After this row transformation aligns $(a,b)$ with any other desired pair, a label permutation aligns the double pair and all the singleton fibers; independent column scalings then align all nonzero representatives. Hence there is one equality type under this larger equivalence.
+
+There are $N(N-1)$ choices of $(a,b)$, $\binom N2$ choices of $J$, $(N-2)!$ bijections $\sigma$, and $(q-1)^N$ choices of the actual nonzero vectors. The unique recovery of these data from a labelled matrix prevents overcounting. Since $\binom N2(N-2)!=N!/2$, their product is the asserted raw count. $\square$
